paras.en: In this he should also be reminded that although on the one hand he ought to keep the book's whole order and method and its particular directions exactly — and the more exactly he keeps them, the more the Lord will concur — nevertheless on the other hand much is left to his prudence, according to the variety of the persons making the Exercises, or of the spirits by which they are moved: so that he may either temper these exercises, or even prescribe certain others suited to their present need, as is plainly said in Annotations 17 and 18 of the opening set, and elsewhere.
paras.note: The Roman numeral references are to the twenty introductory Annotations of the Exercises.

kapitel.label: Cap. IX
kapitel.la_titel: De variis hominum generibus, quibus dari possunt exercitia
kapitel.en_titel: On the various kinds of people to whom the Exercises may be given

paras.la: Quibus exercitia dari possunt, in universum in duas classes dividi posse videntur. Alii enim sunt, qui omnes illas conditiones habent, quas capite primo diximus requiri, ut integra exercitia peragant; et de his nihil hic in particulari dicendum est: ad eos enim pertinent omnia quae toto hoc Directorio dicentur, maxime si de totius vitae statu deliberare velint.
paras.en: Those to whom the Exercises may be given can, broadly speaking, be divided into two classes. Some possess all the qualifications which we said in the first chapter are required for making the Exercises in full; of these nothing particular need be said here, for everything said throughout this Directory applies to them — above all if they wish to deliberate about the state of their whole life.

paras.la: Alii igitur sunt, quibus non sunt tradenda plena exercitia: vel quia iam in statu sunt, ut matrimonio vincti, et alii quibus ob alias causas non expedit dari electionem; vel quia propter negotia publica aliasve occupationes tempus aut locum non habent, ut sunt magistratus, et quidam aliquando nobiles, aut patresfamilias, et similes; vel quia non aliam utilitatem quaerunt ex exercitiis, quam ut generalem confessionem faciant, et ad reliquam vitam bene dirigendam instruantur; vel quia non admodum capaces sunt, ut sunt rudes et illitterati, qui tamen iuvandi sunt iuxta eorum captum.
paras.en: The others are those to whom the full Exercises are not to be given: either because they are already settled in a state, as those bound in marriage, and others to whom for other reasons it is not expedient to give the election; or because on account of public business or other occupations they have neither time nor place, as magistrates, and sometimes nobles, or heads of households, and the like; or because they seek no other profit from the Exercises than to make a general confession and be instructed for the good direction of the rest of their life; or because they are of no great capacity, as the unlettered and untaught — who nevertheless are to be helped according to their measure.

paras.la: Igitur quod attinet ad religiosos (non agimus de nostris, quia de his separatim agemus capite sequenti): si antea nullum mentalis orationis usum habuerunt, eadem est ratio, quod ad eos instruendos attinet, quae alterius cuiusvis saecularis — maxime si antea laxiorem et liberiorem vitam duxissent. Tunc enim diligenter exercendi essent prima hebdomada, ut habeant cognitionem et contritionem suorum peccatorum, tum quae in saeculo, tum quae in religione commiserint, quia hoc est fundamentum ad reformationem et correctionem totius vitae. Si vero antea etiam dediti fuissent orationi mentali et devotioni, tunc prima hebdomada brevius percurri poterit, ut diligentius immorentur in meditatione vitae Christi.
paras.en: As regards religious, then (we do not speak of our own men, of whom we shall treat separately in the following chapter): if they have had no previous practice of mental prayer, the way of instructing them is the same as for any secular person — above all if they have previously led a laxer and freer life. In that case they should be exercised diligently in the First Week, so as to gain knowledge of and contrition for their sins, both those committed in the world and those in religion; for this is the foundation for the reformation and correction of the whole of life. But if they have already been given to mental prayer and devotion, the First Week may be run through more briefly, so that they may dwell the more diligently on the meditation of the life of Christ.

paras.la: Illud vero in prima hebdomada et deinceps praecipue curandum erit: ut in sua vocatione confirmentur, et sibi persuadeant hanc viam sibi constitutam esse ad beatitudinem consequendam; ut regulas sui ordinis plurimi faciant, et eas quam diligentissime observent, et ad suum institutum quam maxime afficiantur; ut causas intelligant quare adhuc minus profecerint, et ad hunc finem meditationes et examina dirigant — quod ab initio explicandum erit, et deinde semper continuandum.
paras.en: In the First Week and thereafter the chief care must be this: that they be confirmed in their vocation, and persuade themselves that this is the way appointed them for attaining blessedness; that they hold the rules of their order in the highest esteem, observe them with all diligence, and grow as attached as possible to their own institute; that they understand the causes why they have hitherto profited less, and direct their meditations and examens to this end — which should be explained at the outset, and continued throughout.

paras.la: Denique etiam ut zelum concipiant iuvandi alios, sive proximos iuxta suum institutum, sive etiam fratres eiusdem instituti, et exemplo et opere.
paras.en: Finally, that they conceive a zeal for helping others — whether their neighbours, according to their institute, or the brethren of their own institute — both by example and by deed.

paras.la: Electio status non est eis danda; sed tamen iuvabit tradere regulas et instructiones eius, ut possint deinde alios iuvare, vel etiam de rebus occurrentibus deliberare, eodem modo quo infra dicetur de hominibus Societatis.
paras.en: The election of a state is not to be given them; but it will nevertheless be helpful to hand on its rules and instructions, so that they may afterwards be able to help others, or even deliberate on matters as they arise, in the same way as will be said below of men of the Society.

paras.la: Quin etiam, finitis exercitiis, posset eis — magno tamen cum delectu et spe fructus, nec sine facultate Provincialis — communicari liber, si ipsi cuperent, et eo bene usuri viderentur; et denique doceri etiam possent de modo tradendi aliis exercitia.
paras.en: Indeed, when the Exercises are over, the book itself might be shared with them — though with great selectiveness and hope of fruit, and not without the Provincial's leave — if they desired it and seemed likely to use it well; and finally they might even be taught the manner of giving the Exercises to others.

paras.la: Ceterum sciant nostri vix fructuosius operam poni posse quam cum religiosis: quoniam non in ipsis tantum fructus ille residet, sed ordinarie manat ad alios — primum quidem ad eorum fratres, qui ipsorum exemplo iuvari possunt, deinde etiam ad saeculares, quorum animas illi tractant. Et ideo licet omnibus religiosis utilia semper sint exercitia, tamen iis maxime, a quibus vel ratione officii vel alterius eiusmodi causae utilitas in alios derivari potest: ut sunt magistri novitiorum, superiores, baccalaurei, concionatores, et alii eiusmodi. Quo fiet saepe, ut uno reformato alii multi reformentur; idque commodius est quam ut nos ipsi id per nos praestemus, ne videamur velle esse aliarum religionum reformatores, quod solet esse odiosum.
paras.en: For the rest, let our men know that labour can hardly be spent more fruitfully than upon religious: for the fruit does not remain in them alone, but ordinarily flows on to others — first to their brethren, who can be helped by their example, and then to the seculars whose souls they have in their care. Hence, though the Exercises are always useful to all religious, they are most useful to those from whom, by reason of office or some similar cause, the benefit can pass on to others: masters of novices, superiors, lecturers, preachers, and the like. Thus it will often happen that when one is reformed many others are reformed too; and this is more fitting than that we should undertake such reform ourselves, lest we seem to want to be reformers of other religious orders — a thing that is wont to give offence.

paras.la: Si sint coniugati aut patresfamilias, dirigenda erunt exercitia ad eum finem: ut iuxta divina praecepta familiam regant, liberos et servos instruant; praeterea ut redditibus et facultatibus iuste ac pie et sobrie utantur, et eleemosynas faciant pro viribus suis, neque excedant in sumptibus; aliaque similia, de quibus agitur in libro Exercitiorum in fine secundae hebdomadae. Hi autem effectus, quos diximus, plerumque solent in anima consequi ex meditationibus ipsis, quanquam alterius materiae: quoniam cum vere timor vel amor Dei ingeneratus fuerit, facile etiam reliqua vita tota reformatur. Sed tamen si instructori videretur propriam aliquam directionem de his dare, vel extra orationem, vel in ipsa oratione per aliquam meditationem, posset etiam hoc fieri; quod idem intelligimus de aliis quoque hominum generibus, de quibus statim dicemus.
paras.en: If they are married men or heads of households, the Exercises are to be directed to this end: that they govern their family according to the divine commandments, and instruct their children and servants; further, that they use their revenues and means justly, piously and soberly, give alms according to their power, and not run to excess in expenditure — and other like matters, treated in the book of the Exercises at the end of the Second Week. These effects of which we have spoken usually follow in the soul from the meditations themselves, though their matter be different: for when the fear or the love of God has truly been engendered, the rest of life too is easily reformed as a whole. Yet if it should seem good to the instructor to give some particular direction on these matters — whether outside prayer, or within prayer itself by means of some meditation — this too could be done; and we mean the same for the other kinds of people of whom we shall speak presently.

paras.la: Si sint ecclesiastici, ita erunt instituendi in exercitiis, ut cognoscant quantam virtutem exigat ille status, eamque acquirere cupiant, et doleant si non hactenus habuerint. Quare ita dirigendi sunt, ut vitia et pravos affectus exuere decernant, et contrariis se virtutibus ornare, quae ecclesiastico homini necessariae sunt; ut semper meminerint se divino cultui et Ecclesiae ministerio dicatos et consecratos esse, ideoque munus suum implere satagant; ut etiam beneficiorum proventus recte dispensare, et in eos usus quos oportet erogare studeant; denique ut etiam zelum Dei habeant, et pro animarum salute iuxta vires et talentum et officium elaborent.
paras.en: If they are ecclesiastics, they are to be so formed in the Exercises that they recognise how great a virtue their state demands, desire to acquire it, and grieve if they have hitherto lacked it. They should therefore be so directed that they resolve to strip off their vices and disordered affections and to adorn themselves with the contrary virtues necessary to a man of the Church; that they remember always that they are dedicated and consecrated to the worship of God and the ministry of the Church, and accordingly strive to fulfil their charge; that they take care also to administer rightly the revenues of their benefices and expend them on their proper uses; and finally that they have the zeal of God, and labour for the salvation of souls according to their strength, their talent and their office.

paras.la: Si sint magnates, aut magistratum aliquem gerant, iis quoque debebunt sua praecepta et documenta tradi: ut iustitiam administrent; ut avaritiam et superbiam fugiant; ut pauperes sublevent; ut se Dei ministros in illo opere esse sentiant; ut semper Dei timorem atque honorem omnibus rebus praeponant; et alia, quae instructor sua prudentia per se videre poterit, et ad ea dirigere eum quem instruit.
paras.en: If they are great men, or hold some magistracy, they too must be given their own precepts and instructions: to administer justice; to flee avarice and pride; to relieve the poor; to feel themselves God's ministers in that work; always to set the fear and honour of God before all things; and whatever else the instructor by his own prudence can see for himself, and direct his charge accordingly.

paras.la: Quod si eiusmodi homines propter publica negotia quae gerunt, vel ob alias honestas causas, non poterunt omnino vacare exercitiis, oportebit accipere quod possunt: ut scilicet aliquas saltem horas quotidie meditationi tribuant. Et tunc etiam poterunt manere in domo sua, ita ut instructor adeat ad ipsos suis temporibus; quod aliquando melius esse posset, quam ut ipsi domum nostram veniant ad instructorem — praesertim cum sunt personae illustriores, quia sic facilius res celatur.
paras.en: But if such men, on account of the public business they conduct or for other honourable reasons, cannot devote themselves entirely to the Exercises, one must take what they can give: namely, that they devote at least some hours daily to meditation. In that case they may also remain in their own house, with the instructor going to them at set times — which may sometimes be better than that they come to our house to the instructor, especially with persons of higher station, since in this way the matter is more easily kept private.
paras.note: The margin cites the Nineteenth Annotation.

paras.la: Illud tamen longe utilius, si possent in aliquod praedium aut coenobium secedere, ut fecit P. M. Ignatius in monte Cassinate. In ipsis autem exercitiis ita procedendum erit, ut res ac tempus postulabit. Nam si minus temporis spatium quotidie impendant meditationi, eo magis proroganda erit prima hebdomada, et confessio generalis, et reliqua. Si vero plures horas meditando insumant, poterunt ista omnia celerius expediri — ut magis vel minus accedatur ad consuetam formam exercitiorum.
paras.en: It would nevertheless be far more useful if they could withdraw to some country estate or monastery — as Father Master Ignatius did at Monte Cassino. In the Exercises themselves one must proceed as the matter and the time demand: if they spend less time daily in meditation, the First Week, the general confession and the rest must be prolonged the more; if they give more hours to meditation, all of this can be despatched more quickly — approaching more or less closely the customary form of the Exercises.

paras.la: His autem electiones non sunt dandae — nisi forte deliberare vellent de officio vel dignitate aliqua suscipienda vel deponenda, aut etiam de vitae statu ii, quibus integrum est. Monendi autem sunt, ut saltem horis illis quibus meditationi vacant, ab omnibus aliarum rerum cogitationibus se expediant, quantum fieri potest.
paras.en: To these the elections are not to be given — unless perhaps they wished to deliberate about taking up or laying down some office or dignity, or even about their state of life, in the case of those still free to do so. They should however be advised that, at least during the hours they give to meditation, they free themselves as far as possible from all thoughts of other things.

paras.la: Si sint rudes et illiterati, non erit multum temporis cum eis insumendum, nec tradenda sunt eis integra exercitia, sed servandus est modus qui indicatur in annotatione 18 ex viginti.
paras.en: If they are untaught and unlettered, not much time should be spent with them, nor are the full Exercises to be given them; the manner indicated in the eighteenth of the twenty Annotations is to be followed.

paras.la: Ad hoc autem caput pertinent etiam feminae, quarum aliquae interdum expetunt exercitia; atque ideo cum iis idem modus servari debet qui cum rudibus — nisi esset aliqua tam bono iudicio, et ita capax rerum spiritualium, tantumque otii domi haberet, ut exacte omnia aut maiorem partem facere possit: tunc enim nihil impediret etiam haec fieri. Sed illud observari deberet, quod prudentiae est: ut ipsae in ecclesiam nostram veniant ad accipiendas meditationes, et ita caute procedatur, ne ulla suspicio aut scandalum sequatur. Quam etiam ob causam fortasse expediet, ut non dentur meditationes in scriptis, sed voce, ne homines existiment aliquas esse epistolas. Quod si scripto utendum erit, fiat omnino discrete.
paras.en: Under this heading come also women, some of whom from time to time ask for the Exercises; with them the same manner should be kept as with the unlettered — unless there were one of such good judgement, so capable in spiritual things, and with so much leisure at home, that she could do everything, or the greater part, exactly: then nothing would prevent this too being done. But what prudence requires should be observed: that they come to our church to receive the meditations, and that matters proceed so cautiously that no suspicion or scandal follow. For the same reason it will perhaps be expedient not to give the meditations in writing but by word of mouth, lest people imagine them to be letters; and if writing must be used, let it be done with entire discretion.

kapitel.label: Cap. X
kapitel.la_titel: De modo tradendi nostris exercitia
kapitel.en_titel: On the manner of giving the Exercises to our own men

paras.la: Quod ad nostros attinet, primum quidem iis qui Societatem ingrediuntur omnino debent dari exercitia omnia integra, et iuxta formam in libro praescriptam. Cum enim hoc sit unum ex experimentis, quod N. P. Ignatius requirit, requiritur etiam ut fiant plane ut iacent — excepta tamen electione — idque singulas meditationes singulis pagellis descriptas quotidie afferendo: neque enim liber ipse dari debet hac prima vice.
paras.en: As regards our own men: first, to those entering the Society the Exercises must be given whole and entire, and according to the form prescribed in the book. For since this is one of the probations which Our Father Ignatius requires, it is required also that they be made exactly as they stand — the election, however, excepted — bringing each day the individual meditations written out on separate slips; for the book itself is not to be given on this first occasion.

paras.la: Praeterea in progressu temporis, cum contigerit se colligant ad facienda exercitia, debebunt haec ipsa aliquoties, ut bis vel ter, facere — si non integre, saltem ea quae sunt primae hebdomadae, et aliquot meditationes ex sequentibus: ut de regno Christi, Incarnatione, tentatione Domini, institutione sanctissimi Sacramenti, Passione, et illa quae est de amore excitando, prout opportunum fuerit, et tempus concesserit.
paras.en: Further, as time goes on, when the occasion comes for them to recollect themselves to make the Exercises, they should make these same Exercises several times — twice or three times — if not entire, at least those of the First Week, together with some meditations from the following Weeks: on the Kingdom of Christ, the Incarnation, the temptation of the Lord, the institution of the most holy Sacrament, the Passion, and the one for stirring up love — as shall be opportune and time shall allow.

paras.la: Quod propterea faciendum est, quia, cum deinde exercitia aliis daturi sint, omnino oportet ut ipsi ea prius bene nota et perspecta sibi fecerint. Quam etiam ob causam oportet, ut praeter meditationes bene intelligant ac teneant usum quarundam regularum et annotationum: v. g. annotationes viginti initio libri exercitiorum positas, examina, additiones decem in fine primae hebdomadae, regulas electionum, discretionis spirituum, et alia eiusmodi. Et ideo legere debebunt librum, et bene intelligere, ac de quo dubitabunt, quaerere ab eo qui eis tradit exercitia.
paras.en: This is to be done because, since they are afterwards to give the Exercises to others, it is altogether necessary that they first make them well known and thoroughly familiar to themselves. For the same reason they ought, beyond the meditations, to understand well and hold the use of certain rules and annotations: for example, the twenty Annotations placed at the beginning of the book of the Exercises, the examens, the ten Additions at the end of the First Week, the rules for the elections and for the discernment of spirits, and other things of the kind. They should therefore read the book and understand it well, and ask about whatever they doubt from the one who gives them the Exercises.

paras.la: Ceterum postquam ea, ut dictum est, aliquando fecerint et repetierint, reliquo deinde tempore, dum nondum ita exercitati erunt in usu meditationum — etsi in quotidianis meditationibus potest quisque pro sua devotione vel necessitate ea meditari quae Dominus suggesserit, ex Evangelio, Scripturis, vel alia (re tamen, pro securiore directione ac utilitate maiore, cum Praefecto rerum spiritualium aut cum Superiore communicata) — tamen cum agitur de tempore aliquo certo meditationibus et secessioni tribuendo, quod nos communiter exercitiorum vocabulo appellamus, quia fere expedit ab aliqua purgatione inchoare, convenit ut aliqua exercitia purgativa non praetermittant: ut de morte, et de peccatis, praesertim reflectendo ad ea quae in religione admiserint.
paras.en: Furthermore, after they have thus made and repeated the Exercises a few times, then in the period that follows, while they are not yet so practised in the use of meditation — although in their daily meditations each may, according to his devotion or need, meditate on what the Lord suggests, from the Gospel, the Scriptures, or elsewhere (the matter, however, being communicated, for safer direction and greater profit, to the Prefect of spiritual things or to the Superior) — nevertheless, when it is a question of a set time given over to meditations and withdrawal, which we commonly call by the name of 'exercises', since it is generally expedient to begin from some purgation, it is fitting that they not omit certain purgative exercises: on death, and on sins, reflecting especially on those they have committed in religion.

paras.la: Neque tamen expedit dare in scriptis exercitia ista accommodata religioso statui: ut exercitia P. N. Ignatii integra, ut sunt, conserventur, nulla re addita vel transformata; ac praeterea quia etiam ipsi maiorem sine dubio gustum et motum sentient ex iis quae ipsimet invenerint, quam quae ab alio ita minute enucleata acceperint. Sed tamen instructor potest aliquam instructionem aut lucem dare, et tanquam in via ponere: monendo eum qui exercetur, ut ipse sibi applicare consuescat — ut v. g. in fundamento, postquam cogitaverit finem hominis, actuet hunc finem in eo statu in quo nunc est: ut quoniam iam non potest esse indifferens ad divitias et paupertatem, applicet hanc indifferentiam ad eas materias quae occurrunt in Societate; et sic de aliis.
paras.en: Nor is it expedient to give out in writing such exercises adapted to the religious state: so that the Exercises of Our Father Ignatius may be preserved whole, as they are, with nothing added or transformed; and moreover because they themselves will without doubt feel greater relish and movement from what they discover for themselves than from what they receive minutely shelled out by another. Yet the instructor may give some instruction or light, and set the exercitant as it were on the road: advising him to accustom himself to make his own applications — for example, in the Foundation, after considering the end of man, to actualise this end in the state in which he now is: since he can no longer be indifferent to riches and poverty, let him apply that indifference to the matters that arise within the Society; and so with the rest.

paras.la: Notandum est etiam, primam hebdomadam debere in nostris, si semel exacte exercitia fecerint, ordinarie satis brevi tempore expediri — ita ut etiam interdum minori spatio quam tridui, vel etiam aliquando bidui expediri possit, si ita videatur — ut gradus fiat ad secundam hebdomadam, in qua ut plurimum diutius immorandum est. Quare hoc potissimum ex instructoris iudicio pendere debebit: qui, si viderit aliquem maiore purgatione indigere, poterit et debebit eum diutius in ea retinere — ante omnia conando, ut eum inducat ad desiderandam sui ipsius reformationem perfectam.
paras.en: It should also be noted that with our own men, if they have once made the Exercises exactly, the First Week should ordinarily be despatched in a fairly short time — indeed sometimes in less than three days, occasionally even in two, if it so seem good — so that passage may be made to the Second Week, on which for the most part one must dwell longer. This must therefore depend chiefly on the instructor's judgement: if he sees that someone needs a greater purgation, he can and should keep him longer in it — striving before all things to bring him to desire his own perfect reformation.

paras.la: Materia autem, circa quam haec reformatio versari debet, haec fere est: passiones non bene domitae, mali habitus, perversae inclinationes — ut ad honorem et aestimationem propriam, vel propriam voluntatem, ad corporis commoditates etc.; tentationes ab extrinseco provenientes, praesertim vehementes et crebrae; deinde etiam ministeria Societatis, ut concionari, audire confessiones, habere scholam; denique omnes actiones quas aliquis componere et ordinare velit, ut comedere, dormire, studere, agere cum externis vel cum nostris, et alia.
paras.en: The matter with which this reformation should deal is roughly this: passions not well tamed; bad habits; perverse inclinations — toward honour and one's own esteem, or one's own will, toward bodily comforts, and so on; temptations coming from without, especially when vehement and frequent; then also the ministries of the Society, such as preaching, hearing confessions, keeping school; and finally all the actions a man may wish to compose and set in order — eating, sleeping, studying, dealing with externs or with our own, and the rest.

paras.la: Quare hoc primum curari debet in eo qui facit exercitia: ut quam maximam sui ipsius acquirat cognitionem, percurrendo tempus ante actum, et occupationes vel officia, et in iis perpendendo tum multitudinem defectuum suorum, tum etiam gravitatem, ratione status et obligationis, tum denique etiam considerando causas et origines et radices eorum vitiorum.
paras.en: The first care, then, with the one making the Exercises must be this: that he acquire the greatest possible knowledge of himself — running over his past life and his occupations or offices, and weighing in them both the multitude of his failings and their gravity, in view of his state and obligation, and finally considering also the causes, origins and roots of those vices.

paras.rub: Pro spirituali reformatione confessio generalis utilis
paras.la: Ad quam etiam reformationem valde utile est, ut in fine primae hebdomadae fiat confessio generalis de toto tempore religionis — non quidem semper, quoties exercitia repetuntur, sed cum aliquis peculiariter motus a Deo vellet instituere novam vitam, seque perfectius reformare. Hoc enim usu compertum est magnopere multis profuisse, et valde iuvisse ad cognitionem sui et emendationem.
paras.en: For this reformation it is also very useful that at the end of the First Week a general confession be made covering the whole time spent in religion — not indeed every time the Exercises are repeated, but when someone, specially moved by God, wishes to begin a new life and reform himself more perfectly. Experience has shown that this has profited many greatly, and helped much toward self-knowledge and amendment.

paras.la: Quod si viderit instructor eum qui exercetur hac ratione iuvandum ad eum finem consequendum qui intenditur, poterit etiam aliquas meditationes statui cuiusque vel necessitati praesenti accommodatas addere: ut de beneficio vocationis, de tribus votis, de causis cur vota renoventur et de ipsa formula votorum nostrorum, de divinis beneficiis, de periculo tepiditatis, et huiusmodi. Interdum etiam ex Summario constitutionum, praesertim ex praecipuis regulis, quibus religiosa fere perfectio continetur, ut 11 et 17 et similes; et in universum eae sint materiae, quae ad timorem et amorem Dei, ad sui ipsius odium, virtutis studium, rerum visibilium contemptum, aeternarum desiderium, atque charitatis ardorem augendum pertinent.
paras.en: If the instructor sees that the exercitant would be helped in this way toward the end intended, he may also add certain meditations suited to each one's state or present need: on the blessing of one's vocation, on the three vows, on the reasons why the vows are renewed and on the very formula of our vows, on the divine benefits, on the danger of tepidity, and the like. Sometimes also from the Summary of the Constitutions, especially from the principal rules in which religious perfection is for the most part contained, such as the 11th and 17th and similar ones. And in general let the matter be such as serves to increase the fear and love of God, hatred of self, zeal for virtue, contempt of visible things, desire of the eternal, and the ardour of charity.

paras.la: Ad faciliorem etiam introductionem eorum, quibus vel non est facultas, vel non vacat per se invenire, poterit via aperiri ad mysteria vitae et passionis Domini, si nonnullae veritates theologicae proponantur: v. g. cum de Incarnatione agitur, si causae eius et fructus explicentur; aut cum de Passione, si causae acerbitatis eius; si etiam insinuentur modi eam meditandi, v. g. ad compatiendum, ad imitandum, ad admirationem; et sic de aliis.
paras.en: Again, for the easier introduction of those who either lack the ability or the leisure to discover things for themselves, a way can be opened into the mysteries of the life and Passion of the Lord by setting out some theological truths: for example, when the Incarnation is treated, by explaining its causes and fruits; or with the Passion, the causes of its bitterness; and by suggesting ways of meditating it — for compassion, for imitation, for admiration; and so with the others.

paras.la: Postremo, qui sunt iam provectiores in rebus spiritualibus, et meditando magis exercitati (de quibus parte 6, cap. 3, § 1): iis, si interdum ad spiritum colligendum et fervorem hauriendum se recipiunt, vel ad aliquod opus aggrediendum, ut missionem aut aliquid eiusmodi — cum nec eadem sit omnium dispositio, nec una mensura — non videtur quicquam praescribendum circa materiam; sed possunt ea meditari, quae sibi utilia putaverint ad eum finem consequendum quem intendunt. Credendum est enim quod ex notitia quam ex exercitiis Patris N. Ignatii antea iam habebant, et ex unctione spiritus adiuti, inoffenso pede, immo magna cum utilitate per hanc viam current.
paras.en: Lastly, for those already more advanced in spiritual things and more practised in meditation (of whom Part VI, chapter 3, § 1 speaks): when from time to time they withdraw to recollect their spirit and draw in fervour, or to undertake some work, such as a mission or the like — since neither is the disposition of all the same, nor is there one measure — it does not seem that anything should be prescribed as to matter; they may meditate on whatever they judge useful for attaining the end they intend. For it is to be believed that with the knowledge they already have from the Exercises of Our Father Ignatius, and helped by the anointing of the Spirit, they will run this way with unstumbling foot — indeed with great profit.

paras.la: Quod attinet ad electionem status, ea non est nostris danda in exercitiis. De electione autem negotii aut actionis alicuius consultare non est proprium exercitiorum, sed potest fieri etiam extra exercitia omni tempore et occasione; et ideo in hac etiam diligenter instruendi sunt nostri, ut sciant bene uti regulis eligendi ad indagandam Dei voluntatem et beneplacitum: ut cum superiores debent statuere de re aliqua dubia, maxime si non possint cum suis consultare, ut dicitur 16. regula Provincialis; et denique in rebus omnibus, quas coram Deo constituere ac definire oporteat, semper admodum iuvat illa praxis quae in eligendo praescribitur, de qua infra prolixius agemus; et inde peti poterunt quae nostros iuvare possint ad intelligendam Dei voluntatem in omni eiusmodi re, iuxta cuiusque rei qualitatem.
paras.en: As for the election of a state, it is not to be given to our own men in the Exercises. But to deliberate about the choice of some business or course of action is not proper to the Exercises alone; it can be done outside them at any time and on any occasion. Our men should therefore be diligently instructed in this too, so that they know how to use well the rules of election for searching out God's will and good pleasure: as when superiors must decide some doubtful matter, especially if they cannot take counsel with their own, as is said in the 16th rule of the Provincial; and in general, in all matters that must be settled and determined before God, that practice which is prescribed for making an election is always of great help — of which we shall treat at greater length below; and from it may be drawn whatever can help our men to understand the will of God in every matter of the kind, according to the nature of each.

kapitel.label: Cap. XI
kapitel.la_titel: De prima hebdomada in universum
kapitel.en_titel: On the First Week in general

paras.la: Omnia haec exercitia a Patre N. Ignatio in quatuor hebdomadas distributa sunt; quae quidem hebdomadae non tam numero dierum quam materiae genere distinguuntur, et ideo non necesse est ut septem vel octo dierum circulus in singulis consumatur, sed sufficit ut illi affectus vel fructus inveniantur, qui in unaquaque exquiruntur.
paras.en: All these Exercises were distributed by Our Father Ignatius into four Weeks; and these Weeks are distinguished not so much by the number of days as by the kind of matter. It is therefore not necessary that a round of seven or eight days be spent on each: it is enough that the affections or fruits be found which are sought in each one.

paras.la: Prima continet considerationem peccatorum, ut eorum foeditatem cognoscamus, vereque detestemur cum dolore et satisfactione convenienti. Secunda proponit vitam Christi ad excitandum in nobis desiderium ac studium eam imitandi; quam imitationem ut melius perficiamus, proponitur etiam modus eligendi vel vitae statum, qui sit maxime ex voluntate Dei, vel, si iam eligi non possit, dantur quaedam monita ad eum in quo quisque sit reformandum. Tertia continet passionem Christi, qua miseratio, dolor, confusio generatur, et illud imitationis desiderium una cum Dei amore vehementius inflammatur. Quarta demum est de Resurrectione Christi eiusque gloriosis apparitionibus, et de beneficiis divinis, et similibus, quae pertinent ad Dei amorem in nobis excitandum.
paras.en: The First contains the consideration of sins, that we may know their foulness and truly detest them, with fitting sorrow and satisfaction. The Second sets forth the life of Christ, to awaken in us the desire and zeal to imitate it; and that we may carry out this imitation the better, there is also proposed the way of electing a state of life that is most according to the will of God — or, if an election can no longer be made, certain counsels are given for reforming the state in which each one is. The Third contains the Passion of Christ, by which compassion, sorrow and confusion are begotten, and that desire of imitation, together with the love of God, is more vehemently inflamed. The Fourth, lastly, concerns the Resurrection of Christ and his glorious apparitions, and the divine benefits, and the like — all of which serve to stir up the love of God in us.

paras.rub: In prima hebdomada sunt media animae purgandae
paras.la: Igitur in hac prima hebdomada proponuntur media, quae ad animam purgandam per contritionem et confessionem pertinent, et ad veram poenitentiam in nobis gignendam iuvare possunt. Quare huc omnia dirigere debet qui facit exercitia: ut peccati malitiam suamque abiectionem et vilitatem agnoscat, eamque ex animo intime sentiat. Quam ob causam expediret, ut hoc tempore, si sacerdos sit, ex hoc spiritu humilitatis abstineat a quotidiana celebratione — nisi devotio, aut profectus spiritualis, aut aliqua obligatio ad id impellat — ut postea, generali confessione peracta, maiori cum praeparatione, fiducia ac reverentia ad sacrificium altaris redeat.
paras.en: In this First Week, then, are proposed the means that serve to purge the soul through contrition and confession, and that can help to beget true penitence in us. To this the one making the Exercises should direct everything: that he may acknowledge the malice of sin and his own abjection and vileness, and feel it inwardly from his heart. For this reason it would be expedient that during this time, if he is a priest, he abstain out of this spirit of humility from daily celebration — unless devotion, or spiritual progress, or some obligation urge him to it — so that afterwards, his general confession made, he may return to the sacrifice of the altar with greater preparation, confidence and reverence.

paras.rub: Hebdomada I, cum sit basis caeterarum, numquam omittenda
paras.la: Notandum etiam hanc primam hebdomadam esse fundamentum ac basim caeterarum, et ideo nunquam praetermitti debere. Unde etiam si quis alias exercitia huius hebdomadae, aut etiam omnia integra fecisset, et denuo ea repetere vellet, tamen hinc incipiendum esset, quamvis brevius expediri posset.
paras.en: It should also be noted that this First Week is the foundation and base of the others, and therefore should never be passed over. Hence even if someone had at another time made the exercises of this Week, or indeed all of them entire, and wished to repeat them anew, he would still have to begin here — though it might be despatched more briefly.

paras.la: Igitur postquam aliquis in eum locum venerit, ubi exercitiis vacaturus est, ea ipsa die debet instructor ad eum adire, et priusquam tradat fundamentum, debet ei explicare aliquas ex annotationibus: nempe primam et quintam, et ex decima septima illam admonitionem de animo aperiendo, item ex vigesima id quod dicitur de utilitate secessus in loco separato. Quod etiam opportunitatem ei dabit, ut eum moneat de iis, quae supra cap. 2 diximus eum esse monendum — cum ea tamen dexteritate quam ibi diximus: nempe ut non omnia simul, sed quantum prudentia dictabit.
paras.en: When, then, someone has come to the place where he is to devote himself to the Exercises, on that very day the instructor should go to him; and before giving the Foundation he should explain to him some of the Annotations — namely the first and the fifth, and from the seventeenth the admonition about opening one's mind, likewise from the twentieth what is said of the usefulness of withdrawing to a separate place. This will also give him the opportunity to advise him of the things of which we said above, in chapter 2, he should be advised — yet with the tact we there described: not everything at once, but as much as prudence dictates.

paras.la: Annotatio autem illa ante fundamentum, quae incipit In primis, expediet magis hoc tempore ut non proponatur ita in genere, quando quis incipit exercitia; sed in discursu exercitiorum, si quid dubium vel obscurum occurrat, aut ob aliquam eius qui exercetur diffidentiam videatur opportunum, tunc ei explicari poterit.
paras.en: As for that annotation placed before the Foundation, which begins In primis, it will be more expedient at this stage not to propose it in general terms when someone is beginning the Exercises; but in the course of the Exercises, if anything doubtful or obscure arises, or it seems opportune because of some diffidence in the exercitant, it can then be explained to him.
paras.note: The reference is to the 'Praesupponendum' (Presupposition) that stands before the Foundation in the book of the Exercises.

kapitel.label: Cap. XII
kapitel.la_titel: De Fundamento
kapitel.en_titel: On the Foundation

paras.rub: De consideratione ultimi finis sive fundamenti
paras.la: Primus ingressus in hanc primam hebdomadam fit per considerationem ultimi finis; quae consideratio ideo dicitur Fundamentum, quia est basis totius aedificii moralis et spiritualis.
paras.en: The first entrance into this First Week is made through the consideration of our last end; and this consideration is called the Foundation, because it is the base of the whole moral and spiritual edifice.

paras.la: Potest autem dividi in tres partes: primo, in finem propter quem homo creatus est; secundo, in media ad consequendum hunc finem; tertio, in difficultatem eligendi hoc vel illud medium, cum ignoremus quid magis aptum sit ad huius finis consecutionem, omnis autem error in hac parte non possit esse non damnosus et periculosus. Ex quo nascetur etiam quartum: ut homo ponat se in illa omnimoda indifferentia et aequilibrio.
paras.en: It can be divided into three parts: first, the end for which man was created; second, the means for attaining this end; third, the difficulty of choosing this or that means, since we do not know which is more apt for reaching this end, while any error in this matter cannot but be harmful and dangerous. From this arises also a fourth point: that a man place himself in that complete indifference and equilibrium.

paras.la: Haec autem indifferentia est maximi momenti, et admonendus est qui se exercet, quanto altius hoc fundamentum iecerit, tanto firmius futurum aedificium; idque etiam indicavit Pater N. Ignatius annotatione decimaquinta et decimasexta ex viginti.
paras.en: This indifference is of the greatest moment, and the exercitant should be advised that the deeper he lays this foundation, the firmer the building will stand; as Our Father Ignatius also indicated in the fifteenth and sixteenth of the twenty Annotations.

paras.rub: Meditatio fundamenti, ne videatur aridior, iuvanda
paras.la: In danda hac meditatione maxime — quia nonnullis, cum nondum assueverint orationi, videri potest aridior — addi poterunt aliquae excursiones ad meditandum: ut in eo quod dicitur creatum esse hominem, potest simul cogitari a Deo esse creatum de nihilo, et simul quot et quanta in creatione habuerit, et praeterea quomodo semper ab illo in esse conservetur.
paras.en: In giving this meditation especially — since to some, not yet accustomed to prayer, it may seem rather dry — certain excursions for meditation may be added: for instance, on the statement that man was created, one may reflect at the same time that he was created by God out of nothing, and likewise how many and how great things he received in creation, and further how he is at every moment preserved in being by him.

paras.la: Sed horum consideratio non tam dirigenda est ad gratitudinem, ut fit cum considerantur beneficia Dei, verum ad scopum huius fundamenti: nempe quod illa omnia a Deo data sint, ut perveniremus ad illum ultimum finem. Unde etiam potest homo in hac meditatione reflectere cogitationem ad seipsum: quomodo hactenus habuerit se ad finem et ad media, quantum aberraverit, quod creaturis abusus sit, quae illi adiumento esse debuerunt — ut iam quasi in generali iaciat fundamenta ad cognoscendam deformitatem vitae suae, quod postea uberius et magis particulariter faciet in meditatione peccatorum.
paras.en: But the consideration of these things is to be directed not so much toward gratitude, as when the benefits of God are considered, but toward the aim of this Foundation: namely, that all those things were given by God so that we might come to that last end. Hence in this meditation a man may also turn his thought back upon himself: how he has hitherto stood toward the end and the means, how far he has strayed, how he has abused the creatures that ought to have been his helps — so that already, as it were in general, he may lay the groundwork for knowing the deformity of his own life, which afterwards he will do more fully and more particularly in the meditation on sins.

paras.la: In meditatione huius fundamenti liber exercitiorum non praescribit certas horas, ut fit in exercitiis sequentibus; sed ut facili initio inchoemus, unusquisque pro viribus et pro devotione sua ad id tempus sibi assumat, vel, si opus sit, instructor ei praescribat.
paras.en: For the meditation on this Foundation the book of the Exercises does not prescribe fixed hours, as it does in the exercises that follow; but so that we may begin with an easy start, let each take for it such time as his strength and devotion allow — or, if need be, let the instructor prescribe it for him.

paras.la: Debet autem curare ut cognitio huius veritatis, quae in fundamento tractatur, quam maxime menti infigatur: quoniam ut fundamentum fabricae totam ipsam sustinet, ita haec veritas influit in omnia exercitia, et praesertim in ipsam electionem status, quae tota fere hinc pendet; et ideo quo melius haec meditatio successerit, eo etiam melius reliqua succedunt.
paras.en: He should take care that the knowledge of this truth treated in the Foundation be fixed in the mind as deeply as possible: for as the foundation of a building bears the whole structure, so this truth flows into all the Exercises, and especially into the election of a state of life itself, which depends almost entirely upon it. The better this meditation succeeds, therefore, the better all the rest succeed as well.

kapitel.label: Cap. XIII
kapitel.la_titel: De duplici examine
kapitel.en_titel: On the twofold examen

paras.rub: Quid faciendum instructori tempore meditationis fundamenti
paras.la: Dum durat meditatio fundamenti, debet instructor exercitantem aliquoties visitare, et semper ei aliquid novi in scriptis afferre: quia sic videtur quodammodo levari taedium, et melius etiam percipi quae singula proponuntur.
paras.en: While the meditation on the Foundation lasts, the instructor should visit the exercitant several times, and always bring him something new in writing: for in this way the tedium seems in some measure relieved, and the several things proposed are also better taken in.

paras.la: Igitur in primo congressu post datum fundamentum datur examen particulare; in quo tradendo significandum est ei, in quovis homine unum aut alterum vitium sive peccatum esse solere praecipuum, et quod in eo sit quasi causa et radix aliorum.
paras.en: In the first meeting after the Foundation has been given, then, the Particular Examen is given. In imparting it he should be told that in every man some one vice or sin is usually the chief, and that it is in him as it were the cause and root of the others.

paras.la: Et licet in aliquo plura essent praecipua, expedire tamen ut unum deligatur, ad quod extirpandum toti incumbamus; ut eo superato ad aliud, et aliud deinceps, peculiarem hunc conatum et studium transferamus.
paras.en: And even if in someone several were chief, it is still expedient that one be chosen, to whose uprooting we apply ourselves wholly; so that when it is overcome we may transfer this special effort and zeal to another, and then to another in turn.

paras.la: Huic igitur rei servit examen particulare, cuius usus, etsi post peracta exercitia esse debet toto vitae tempore, nunc tamen inchoatur: tum ut aliqua eius peritia acquiratur, tum etiam quia hoc examine uti oportet circa exercitia et eorum additiones.
paras.en: To this purpose, then, serves the Particular Examen. Its use, though after the Exercises are finished it should continue for the whole of life, is nevertheless begun now: both that some skill in it may be acquired, and also because this examen must be used upon the exercises themselves and their Additions.

paras.la: Est autem multum commendandus huius examinis usus propter magnam eius utilitatem, praesertim ad consequendam animi puritatem, ut docet Cassianus, Collatione 4 et 5, Bernardus saepe. Itaque in fine exercitiorum, cum discedenti dantur praecepta vitae bene instituendae, hoc in primis inculcandum est. Additiones autem illae quatuor dictandae ne sint, an verbo tantum explicandae, prudentiae instructoris relinquatur.
paras.en: The use of this examen is much to be commended for its great usefulness, especially for attaining purity of soul, as Cassian teaches in Conferences 4 and 5, and Bernard often. Hence at the end of the Exercises, when precepts for ordering his life well are given to the one departing, this is to be urged before all else. Whether those four Additions should be dictated, or only explained by word of mouth, is left to the prudence of the instructor.
paras.note: Margin: 'Cassianus Collat. 4 et 5.'

paras.la: Deinde eadem die, et sequenti, datur examen generale et quotidianum. Non autem datur per modum meditationis, sed instructionis cuiusdam, et ut homo incipiat aperire oculos ad cognoscenda peccata vitae praeteritae.
paras.en: Then, on the same day and the following, the General and the Daily Examen are given. They are given not by way of meditation, but as a kind of instruction, and so that a man may begin to open his eyes to recognize the sins of his past life.

paras.la: Quod vero attinet ad examen generale: non est dubium quin aliae etiam multae sint peccatorum species, quae hic non ponuntur. Sed vel hic ea tantum peccata attinguntur, quae frequentius accidunt — reliqua autem peti possunt ab aliis auctoribus, qui ex professo de hoc agunt — vel hoc examen pro iis tantum conscriptum est, qui iam paulo magis spirituales sunt et ab aliis gravioribus peccatis abstinent, in haec autem frequentius incidere solent. Itaque non fuit mens P. N. Ignatii tam brevi tractatione omnia peccata comprehendere, sed tantum, ut dictum est, pios animos admonere de iis quae frequentiora sunt.
paras.en: As regards the General Examen: there is no doubt that there are many other kinds of sins besides which are not set down here. But either only those sins are touched on here which occur more frequently — the rest may be sought from other authors who treat of this professedly — or this examen was written only for those who are already somewhat more spiritual and abstain from other graver sins, yet are wont to fall more frequently into these. It was therefore not the mind of Our Father Ignatius to comprehend all sins in so brief a treatment, but only, as has been said, to admonish devout souls about those that are more frequent.
paras.note: OCR 'Hgunt' emended to 'agunt'.

paras.la: Porro examen quotidianum, quod quinque puncta complectitur, dictetur prout iacet. Ad illud autem faciendum iuvat illa lux, quam praebet examen generale per illam distinctionem peccatorum, quae fiunt cogitatione, locutione et opere.
paras.en: Further, the Daily Examen, which comprises five points, should be dictated just as it stands. In making it, that light is a help which the General Examen affords through its distinction of sins committed in thought, word and deed.

kapitel.label: Cap. XIV
kapitel.la_titel: De primo exercitio primae hebdomadae
kapitel.en_titel: On the first exercise of the First Week

paras.la: Circa ordinem tradendi exercitia sequendus est is qui ponitur in ipso libro exercitiorum: nempe ut prima hora fiat exercitium trium potentiarum, secunda autem peccatorum, tertia vero et quarta repetitiones utriusque. Si autem addatur etiam quinta hora, fiat de inferno. Sin fiant tantum quatuor horae, hoc exercitium de inferno differendum erit in diem sequentem; quo eodem die possunt dari etiam alia exercitia de morte, de iudicio, cum suis repetitionibus. Tertio die proponenda erit eadem materia, sed cum aliquibus novis punctis: ut in materia peccati, proponendo effectus quos facit in animo, aut aliquid eiusmodi; sic enim tollitur taedium, et materiae profundius penetrantur.
paras.en: As to the order of giving the exercises, that order should be followed which is set down in the book of the Exercises itself: namely, that at the first hour be made the exercise of the Three Powers, at the second that on sins, and at the third and fourth the repetitions of both. If a fifth hour is added, let it be on hell. But if only four hours are made, this exercise on hell will have to be deferred to the following day; on which same day other exercises may also be given, on death and on judgment, with their repetitions. On the third day the same matter is to be proposed, but with some new points — as, in the matter of sin, by proposing the effects it works in the soul, or something of that kind; for in this way tedium is removed, and the matters are penetrated more deeply.

paras.la: Porro primum exercitium illud est quod appellatur trium potentiarum: non quia in aliis etiam non exerceantur hae tres potentiae, sed voluit P. N. Ignatius in hoc quasi aditu et principio omnium exercitiorum viam monstrare, quae in meditando tenenda est — nempe ut per memoriam adiuvaretur ratio ad discurrendum sive ratiocinandum, per discursum autem excitaretur voluntas et affectus; idque actuare voluit in materia peccati, quae prima occurrebat ad meditandum.
paras.en: Now the first exercise is that which is called the exercise of the Three Powers: not that these three powers are not exercised in the others as well, but Our Father Ignatius wished, in this entrance-way and beginning of all the Exercises, to show the way to be kept in meditating — namely, that by the memory the reason should be helped to discourse, or reason, and by the discourse the will and the affections should be stirred; and he chose to put this into practice in the matter of sin, which was the first that came up for meditation.

paras.la: Itaque in hoc primo exercitio sunt sigillatim explicanda exercitia sumenti omnia, quae in sequentibus exercitiis futura sunt usui: quis scilicet modus servandus, ut cum attentione et sine capitis laesione perseverari possit; et quomodo se animus colligere collectumque tenere debeat; et quod, licet adhibendus sit intellectus ad cogitandum, maior tamen habenda est cura affectus et interioris gustus, quam ut multi conceptus quantumvis pulchri et acuti formentur; et alia eiusmodi.
paras.en: In this first exercise, therefore, everything is to be explained one by one to the person taking the Exercises which will be of use in the exercises that follow: namely, what manner is to be kept so that he can persevere with attention and without injury to the head; how the soul should recollect itself and keep itself recollected; and that although the understanding must be applied to thinking, greater care is nevertheless to be taken for the affections and inward relish than for forming many concepts, however beautiful and acute; and other things of this kind.

paras.la: Tum etiam declaranda sunt praeludia, quorum usus praescribitur in omnibus exercitiis; et in primis quid sit compositio loci, quae nihil aliud est quam fingere sibi et quasi videre oculis imaginationis locum illum, in quo res quam meditamur gesta est: ut stabulum in quo Christus natus est, aut coenaculum grande stratum in quo Apostolorum pedes lavit, aut montem in quo passus est.
paras.en: Then the preludes are also to be explained, whose use is prescribed in all the exercises; and first of all, what the composition of place is — which is nothing other than to picture to oneself, and as it were see with the eyes of the imagination, the place where the thing we are meditating on took place: such as the stable in which Christ was born, or the large furnished upper room in which he washed the feet of the Apostles, or the mount on which he suffered.

paras.la: Hac enim loci compositione valde iuvamur ad attentionem et motionem animae, quae hoc modo, quasi alligata phantasia rei illi certae, alligatur ipsa quoque quodammodo ne evagetur; aut si quando divertat, habet ad manum quo se facile colligat, et revocet in situm illum suum, in quo se ab initio composuit. Unde S. Bonaventura in prooemio de vita Christi: Tu, inquit, si fructum ex his sumere cupis, ita te praesentem exhibeas iis quae per D. N. Iesum Christum dicta et facta narrantur, ac si tuis oculis ea videres et tuis auribus audires, toto mentis affectu, diligenter, delectabiliter et morose, omnibus aliis curis et solicitudinibus tuis omissis.
paras.en: By this composition of place we are greatly helped toward attention and the movement of the soul: for in this way, the imagination being as it were bound to that definite thing, the soul too is in some manner bound, lest it wander; or if at times it strays, it has at hand a means of easily recollecting itself and returning to that station in which it settled itself at the beginning. Hence St. Bonaventure, in the preface of the Life of Christ, says: If you desire to draw fruit from these things, make yourself present to what is related as said and done by Our Lord Jesus Christ, as though you saw it with your own eyes and heard it with your own ears — with the whole affection of your mind, diligently, delightfully and lingeringly, laying aside all your other cares and anxieties.
paras.note: The quotation is from the Meditationes vitae Christi, then commonly attributed to St. Bonaventure.

paras.la: Atque hoc quidem locum habet in meditatione rerum corporearum; nam in rebus incorporeis, ut est peccatum et similia, alia quaedam est instituenda compositio loci, de qua dicitur satis clare in libro exercitiorum, in exercitio trium potentiarum.
paras.en: This, indeed, holds for the meditation of corporeal things; for in incorporeal things, such as sin and the like, a different kind of composition of place is to be made, of which enough is said clearly in the book of the Exercises, in the exercise of the Three Powers.

paras.la: Denique in hac loci repraesentatione vitandum est diligenter, ne nimis in ea fabricanda immoremur, vel nimiam vim capiti faciamus: quia non consistit in ea fructus praecipuus meditationis, sed est tantum via et instrumentum ad ipsum fructum. Nec est dubium quin aliqui maiorem in hac re habeant facilitatem, in quibus videlicet acrior est vis potentiae imaginativae; alii vero, quibus hoc difficilius est, non ita laborare debent ut caput obtundant, quo ipsam meditationem impedirent.
paras.en: Finally, in this representation of place one must carefully avoid dwelling too long on its construction, or doing too much violence to the head: for the chief fruit of the meditation does not consist in it — it is only a way and an instrument to the fruit itself. Nor is there any doubt that some have a greater facility in this, those namely in whom the power of imagination is keener; while others, for whom it is more difficult, ought not to labour at it so as to batter their heads and thereby hinder the meditation itself.

kapitel.label: Cap. XV
kapitel.la_titel: De aliis exercitiis primae hebdomadae
kapitel.en_titel: On the other exercises of the First Week

paras.rub: In secundo exercitio de quo monendus exercitans
paras.la: In secundo exercitio, in primo puncto, monendus est exercitans ne descendat ad examinanda peccata sigillatim, ut fieri solet cum quis se ad confessionem parat — hoc enim postea facturus est extra meditationem — sed hoc tempore in genere tantum proponat sibi sua peccata eorumque multitudinem et magnitudinem, ut concipiat confusionem et dolorem. Ad hoc autem confert percurrere loca, negotia et personas, ut hic dicitur.
paras.en: In the second exercise, at the first point, the exercitant should be advised not to descend to examining his sins one by one, as is usually done when someone is preparing for confession — for this he will do later, outside the meditation — but at this time only to set before himself his sins in general, their multitude and their greatness, so that he may conceive confusion and sorrow. For this it helps to run through the places, occupations and persons, as is said here.

paras.la: Tertium et quartum exercitium constat ex repetitione primi et secundi. Harum autem repetitionum usus est valde utilis: saepe enim fit, ut cum eiusmodi materiae primum cogitantur, intellectus pascatur illa rerum novitate ac curiositate quadam; postea vero, cum speculationem moderamur, magis aperitur via internis affectibus, in quibus potissimum consistit fructus. Quare in his repetitionibus vitandi sunt longi discursus; sed tantum proponere sibi oportet, et quasi percurrere, quae prius meditati sumus, et in iis immorandum voluntate et affectu. Et haec etiam est causa cur plura hic colloquia sint, quam in prioribus exercitiis.
paras.en: The third and fourth exercises consist in the repetition of the first and second. The use of these repetitions is very profitable: for it often happens that when such matters are first thought upon, the understanding feeds on the novelty of the things and on a certain curiosity; but afterwards, when we moderate the speculation, the way is opened wider to the inward affections, in which the fruit chiefly consists. In these repetitions, therefore, long discourses are to be avoided; one should only set before oneself, and as it were run through, what we meditated before, and dwell in it with the will and the affections. This is also the reason why there are more colloquies here than in the earlier exercises.

paras.la: Quod autem dicitur in libro exercitiorum, in tertio exercitio primae hebdomadae, repetitionem hanc faciendam de iis in quibus antea maiorem consolationem aut desolationem senserimus, ita intelligendum est: ut praecipue repeti debeant ea quae lumen aut fervorem attulerunt; sed etiam expedit illa puncta repetere in quibus ariditatem sensimus, quia saepe contingit ut deinde in ipsis maiorem consolationis copiam sentiamus. Immo etiam bis repeti potest idem, si magna sentitur consolatio, aut alius bonus et spiritualis affectus; et hoc potissimum in prima hebdomada.
paras.en: As for what is said in the book of the Exercises, in the third exercise of the First Week — that this repetition is to be made on those points in which we previously felt greater consolation or desolation — it is to be understood thus: chiefly those points should be repeated which brought light or fervour; but it is also expedient to repeat those points in which we felt dryness, for it often happens that in these we afterwards feel a greater abundance of consolation. Indeed, the same may even be repeated twice, if great consolation is felt, or some other good and spiritual affection; and this above all in the First Week.

paras.la: Praeter quinque haec exercitia P. N. Ignatii possunt addi alia, ut in fine quinti exercitii dicitur: ut de aliis peccati poenis, de morte, de iudicio, vel de aliis cruciatibus inferni. Et quidem haec rarissime omittenda videntur, quia multum habent momenti ut avocetur animus ab inordinato amore rerum harum visibilium; et in his meditationibus concipit anima timorem sanctum Domini, ut pariat spiritum salutis.
paras.en: Besides these five exercises of Our Father Ignatius others may be added, as is said at the end of the fifth exercise: on the other penalties of sin, on death, on judgment, or on the other torments of hell. And these, indeed, seem very rarely to be omitted, for they carry much weight in calling the soul away from the inordinate love of these visible things; and in these meditations the soul conceives the holy fear of the Lord, that it may bring forth the spirit of salvation.

paras.la: In fine cuiuslibet exercitii semper fieri debet colloquium, ut in libro exercitiorum praescribitur; nec tamen prohibetur quin iuxta cuiusque devotionem etiam in principio et in medio alia colloquia et petitiones fieri possint — immo etiam aliquando expedit. Proprius tamen locus est in fine, cum anima ex meditatione magis elevatam se sentit. Illa enim sunt aptissima colloquia, quae formantur ex affectu interiori — varia, ut ipse affectus varius est.
paras.en: At the end of every exercise a colloquy should always be made, as is prescribed in the book of the Exercises; yet it is not forbidden that, according to each one's devotion, other colloquies and petitions be made also at the beginning and in the middle — indeed at times it is even expedient. The proper place, however, is at the end, when the soul feels itself more lifted up by the meditation. For those colloquies are the most fitting which are formed out of the inward affection — varied, as the affection itself varies.

paras.la: Interdum enim homo agit cum Deo ut filius cum patre, interdum ut servus cum domino, modo ut amicus cum amico, modo etiam ut reus cum iudice; aliquando etiam petens aliquod donum, aliquando gratias agens de beneficiis acceptis, alias accusando seipsum, alias communicando cum eo familiariter.
paras.en: For sometimes a man deals with God as a son with his father, sometimes as a servant with his lord, now as a friend with a friend, now again as a defendant with his judge; sometimes too asking some gift, sometimes giving thanks for benefits received, at other times accusing himself, at others conversing with him familiarly.
paras.note: Margin cross-reference: 'Ex 1. exercitio primae hebdomadae.'

paras.la: In quo notandum quod dicitur in tertia annotatione ex viginti: haec colloquia, quando fiunt cum Deo aut cum sanctis, requirere maiorem reverentiam quam ipsas meditationes et speculationes. In particulari vero colloquium secundum, ad Christum ut impetret a Patre, explicandum erit rudioribus hoc intelligi non ut est Deus, sed ut homo mediator et advocatus, ut interpellet pro nobis.
paras.en: Here should be noted what is said in the third of the twenty Annotations: that these colloquies, when they are made with God or with the saints, require greater reverence than the meditations and speculations themselves. In particular, the second colloquy — to Christ, that he may obtain from the Father — will have to be explained to the less instructed as addressed to him not as he is God, but as man, mediator and advocate, that he may intercede for us.

paras.la: Additiones, quae in libro exercitiorum ponuntur in fine primae hebdomadae, dandae sunt pridie quam incipiantur exercitia — nempe meditatio quae dicitur trium potentiarum, et reliquae — quia in iis agitur de multis quae adiuvant meditationem. Decima tamen additio posset differri in sequentem diem, quia non est adeo necessarium ut detur illo die. Deinde sequentibus diebus dandae sunt reliquae additiones, et regulae de discernendis spiritibus quae conveniunt primae hebdomadae, et quae convenire videbuntur exercitanti; quas tamen non erit semper necesse scripto dare, sed id instructoris iudicio permittitur.
paras.en: The Additions, which in the book of the Exercises are placed at the end of the First Week, are to be given on the day before the exercises begin — that is, before the meditation called that of the Three Powers, and the rest — because they treat of many things that assist meditation. The tenth Addition, however, could be deferred to the following day, since it is not so necessary that it be given on that day. Then on the following days are to be given the remaining Additions, and those Rules for the Discernment of Spirits which belong to the First Week and which shall seem suited to the exercitant; yet it will not always be necessary to give these in writing — that is left to the judgment of the instructor.

paras.la: Hae additiones curandum est ut exacte serventur, quia ex ipsis valde pendet fructus spiritualis exercitiorum. Quamquam ex altera parte caveri etiam debet omnis excessus, et habenda est ratio personarum et complexionum: ut si qui essent natura melancholici, non debent nimium coarctari, immo potius dilatandus est eis animus; et idem de personis imbecillioris valetudinis et insuetis ad hos labores. Et ideo opus est prudentia et discretione: experientia enim ostendit quibusdam profuisse quod eis concederetur aliqua laxitas in his regulis servandis, aliis autem profuit severitas et rigor — semper tamen mixtus suavitate.
paras.en: Care should be taken that these Additions be exactly observed, for the spiritual fruit of the Exercises depends greatly upon them. Yet on the other hand every excess must also be guarded against, and regard must be had for persons and temperaments: those who are melancholic by nature should not be too much constricted — rather their spirit should be given room; and the same for persons of weaker health, or unaccustomed to these labours. Prudence and discretion are therefore needed: for experience shows that some have profited by being allowed a certain laxity in keeping these rules, while for others severity and rigour have profited — yet always tempered with gentleness.

kapitel.label: Cap. XVI
kapitel.la_titel: De confessione generali
kapitel.en_titel: On the general confession

paras.la: Cum is qui se exercet versetur in primis quinque exercitiis, sive alia adiungantur, cum iam id satis consecutus videbitur quod in hac hebdomada ut finis proponitur — nimirum cognitionem intimam peccatorum et veram contritionem — et ad id serio conatus et divinae gratiae cooperatus, tam per exercitia quam per additiones, iudicabitur, moneri debet ut se ad generalem confessionem disponat. Et nisi instructori nimium fatigatus videatur, poterit adhuc pergere in meditando per unam aut alteram horam aliquid quod ad compunctionem peccatorum faciat, vel, si id magis expedire iudicetur, aliquid legendo ad eum finem.
paras.en: While the exercitant is occupied with the first five exercises, or with others added to them, once he shall be judged to have sufficiently attained what is proposed as the end of this Week — namely, an intimate knowledge of his sins and true contrition — having seriously striven for it and cooperated with divine grace, both through the exercises and through the Additions, he should be advised to dispose himself for a general confession. And unless he seems to the instructor too much fatigued, he may still continue meditating, for an hour or two, on something conducive to compunction for his sins — or, if this be judged more expedient, reading something to that end.

paras.la: Ut autem hoc diligentius et accuratius faciat, indicandum est ei quantae sint utilitates huius confessionis generalis, de quibus utilitatibus agitur in ipso libro exercitiorum post examen generale. Quod si nulla alia esset, hoc certe satis esse deberet: quod experimur homines plerumque aut sine examine sufficienti, aut sine debito dolore, nullo vel valde infirmo melioris vitae proposito, ad confessionem accedere; ac propterea, ad consequendam pacem conscientiae, et ad tollendos scrupulos — qui, si non antea, saltem in puncto mortis animam excruciare et in periculum salutis aeternae adducere solent — multum prodest semel se ab omnibus anteactae vitae peccatis abluere.
paras.en: That he may do this the more diligently and carefully, he should be shown how great are the benefits of this general confession, which benefits are treated in the book of the Exercises itself, after the General Examen. Even if there were no other, this surely ought to suffice: that we find men for the most part come to confession either without sufficient examination, or without due sorrow, with no purpose of a better life or a very feeble one; and therefore, for gaining peace of conscience and removing scruples — which, if not before, at least at the point of death are wont to torment the soul and bring it into danger of eternal salvation — it profits much to wash oneself once for all from all the sins of one's past life.

paras.rub: Quae diligentia servanda in huiusmodi confessione
paras.la: Quam etiam ob causam, etsi cavendum est a nimia anxietate in facienda hac confessione, ne semper deinde maneant scrupuli ac reliquiae, ut quibusdam contingit, tamen ex altera parte studendum et conandum est ut ita diligenter atque accurate fiat, ut postea secura esse possit anima se fecisse quod in se erat: nam sine hoc numquam frui poterit illa pace animi et tranquillitate conscientiae quam diximus. Ideo praeter proprium studium et diligentiam ipsius qui exercitia suscipit, iuvandus est etiam aliqua via et methodo: nempe directorio aliquo ad bene confitendum, cuiusmodi iam multa extant bona et apta, si opus fuerit, et pro cuiusque indigentia.
paras.en: For this reason also, although excessive anxiety in making this confession is to be avoided, lest scruples and residues remain ever after, as happens to some, yet on the other hand one must study and strive that it be made so diligently and carefully that afterwards the soul can be secure that it has done what lay in it: for without this it will never be able to enjoy that peace of soul and tranquillity of conscience of which we have spoken. Therefore, besides the personal effort and diligence of the one undertaking the Exercises, he should also be helped by some way and method: namely, by some directory for confessing well — of which many good and apt ones now exist — if there be need, and according to each one's want.

paras.la: Aliquando etiam, praesertim insignioribus hominibus, proderit dare legendam Summam Navarri, ubi agit de statibus, ut attente considerent quae ad suum statum pertinent. Sic enim melius videbunt in quibus defecerint; quae si nostri per se proponerent, fortasse non tantam iis fidem haberent, et possent putare eos esse nimios in urgendis conscientiis.
paras.en: Sometimes also, especially with men of higher station, it will be profitable to give them to read the Summa of Navarrus, where he treats of the states of life, that they may attentively consider what pertains to their own state. In this way they will see better wherein they have failed; whereas if our men were to propose these things themselves, perhaps they would not be given so much credit, and might be thought excessive in pressing consciences.
paras.note: The 'Summa of Navarrus' is the widely used confessors' manual (Enchiridion sive Manuale confessariorum) of Martín de Azpilcueta, 'Doctor Navarrus'.

paras.la: Hanc generalem confessionem ut plurimum magis expedit non fieri ei qui tradit exercitia; si tamen qui suscipit ei confiteri mallet pro sua devotione, vel sacerdotum penuria aut aliae causae ita exigerent, nihil impediret quin etiam ipsi fieri posset.
paras.en: For the most part it is more expedient that this general confession not be made to the one who is giving the Exercises; yet if the one undertaking them should prefer, out of his own devotion, to confess to him, or if scarcity of priests or other causes should so require, nothing would prevent its being made to him as well.

kapitel.label: Cap. XVII
kapitel.la_titel: De fine primae hebdomadae
kapitel.en_titel: On the end of the First Week

paras.rub: Primae hebdomadae tempus quando contrahendum aut prorogandum
paras.la: Quoniam, ut supra dictum est, exercitiorum hebdomadae non dierum spatio definiuntur, sed ex effectu qui in eis praetenditur, ideo huius primae hebdomadae tempus vel contrahi vel prorogari poterit, prout citius vel tardius quis contritionem, devotionem, vel meditandi modum assecutus fuerit; alii enim celerius, alii serius eo perveniunt. Illud tamen notandum: eos homines qui multum proficiunt in via spiritus, et qui iam ab aliquo tempore sacramenta frequentant, aut qui multum cupiunt statuere de modo vitae suae, in quo magis Deo Domino servire possint, non esse diu detinendos in hac prima hebdomada — immo, si fieri possit, quatuor aut quinque diebus absolvere eam debent. Contra vero faciendum in iis qui non ita dispositi sunt: hi enim, ut peccata sua defleant, et ut peccati turpitudinem ac foeditatem agnoscant, debent diutius in his exerceri, mutando subinde rationem victus somnique, et alia genera paenitentiae, ut habetur in exercitiis, notabili tertio post additiones primae hebdomadae.
paras.en: Since, as was said above, the Weeks of the Exercises are not defined by a span of days but by the effect aimed at in them, the time of this First Week may be shortened or prolonged according as one attains contrition, devotion, or the manner of meditating sooner or later; for some arrive at it more quickly, others more slowly. Yet this should be noted: those who are making much progress in the way of the spirit, and who have already for some time been frequenting the sacraments, or who greatly desire to decide upon a manner of life in which they can serve God our Lord better, should not be kept long in this First Week — indeed, if it can be done, they ought to finish it in four or five days. The contrary is to be done with those who are not so disposed: these, that they may weep over their sins and recognize the baseness and foulness of sin, should be exercised longer in these matters, varying from time to time their regimen of food and sleep, and the other kinds of penance, as is set down in the Exercises, in the third note after the Additions of the First Week.

paras.la: Qui, absolutis exercitiis primae hebdomadae, ad reliqua progressurus est, postquam generaliter confessus fuerit et communionem sumpserit, saltem per unum diem vacare debet ab illo labore tam intense meditandi. Interim tamen posset in mente versare parabolam illam filii prodigi, applicando eam ad seipsum, aut aliquid eiusmodi. Porro ad communionem est ita etiam disponendus, ut ad eam accedat cum reverentia et fide et gustu; et ob eam causam danda est ei aliqua meditatio ad hoc apta.
paras.en: He who, having finished the exercises of the First Week, is to go on to the rest, after he has made his general confession and received Communion, should rest for at least one day from that labour of such intense meditating. Meanwhile, however, he might turn over in his mind the parable of the prodigal son, applying it to himself, or something of that kind. Further, he is also to be so disposed for Communion that he approach it with reverence and faith and relish; and for that reason some meditation apt for this should be given him.

kapitel.label: Cap. XVIII
kapitel.la_titel: De secunda hebdomada, et primo de fine qui in ea praetenditur
kapitel.en_titel: On the Second Week, and first on the end aimed at in it

paras.la: Finis et scopus, qui exercitiis omnibus primae hebdomadae praefixus est, hic praecipue est: cognoscere quod erravimus ab ea via quae nos ducere debebat ad ultimum illum finem cuius causa creati sumus; et consequenter dolere de tali et tanto errore, et concipere intensum desiderium redeundi in illam viam et in ea semper perseverandi.
paras.en: The end and aim set before all the exercises of the First Week is chiefly this: to know that we have strayed from the way that was to lead us to that last end for which we were created; and consequently to grieve over so great and such an error, and to conceive an intense desire of returning to that way and of persevering in it always.

paras.la: In hac autem secunda hebdomada finis est proponere sibi Christum Dominum ac Salvatorem nostrum ut veram viam, iuxta illud quod ipse dixit: Ego sum via, veritas et vita; et: Nemo venit ad Patrem nisi per me (Ioan. 14, 6). Ipse enim est exemplar a Patre hominibus propositum, cuius imitatione emendemus et componamus mores nostros corruptos, et dirigamus pedes nostros in viam pacis. Quare, cum Christi vita sit perfectissima et ipsa idea virtutis et sanctitatis, sequitur ut, quo vita nostra propius ad eam imitatione accesserit, ipsa quoque perfectior sit — immo et propius accedat ad ultimum finem suum, ideoque eo etiam felicior sit.
paras.en: In this Second Week the end is to set before oneself Christ our Lord and Saviour as the true way, according to his own words: I am the way, the truth and the life; and: No one comes to the Father except through me (John 14:6). For he is the exemplar set before men by the Father, by whose imitation we are to amend and order our corrupted conduct, and direct our feet into the way of peace.
