Nam alioquin non posset homo indifferens esse ad eam retinendam vel relinquendam, quod tamen dicitur in tertia classe.
paras.en: For the better understanding of these three classes, it should be noted that in all of them this is presupposed: that the manner in which the money was acquired was not illicit, so as to oblige to restitution. For otherwise a man could not be indifferent about keeping or leaving it — which nevertheless is said of the third class.

paras.la: Est ergo hic modus: ut quando v. g. aliquis ex nimio studio lucri, vel ex aliquo alio affectu humano et vitioso, negociatur. Secundo notandum: primam et secundam classem ita inter se differre, quod utraque habet quidem voluntatem quandam infirmam et remissam exuendi affectum ad rem illam; sed prima classis nulla unquam adhibet media, nec cogitat de mediis; secunda vero aliquid amplius facit, quia adhibet quidem aliqua media, sed quae ipsi placent, non autem iuxta Dei voluntatem ac beneplacitum, et ideo videtur sibi parata omnia alia facere praeter illud, ut privetur re illa quam amat. Tertia porro ad hoc etiam parata est, si Deo ita placeat; idque tantum inquirit, an placeat.
paras.en: The case, then, is of this kind: as when, for example, someone trades out of an excessive eagerness for gain, or from some other human and vicious affection. Second, it should be noted that the first and second classes differ from each other thus: both indeed have a certain weak and slack will to put off their attachment to the thing; but the first class never applies any means, nor thinks of means; the second does something more, for it does apply certain means — but such as please itself, not such as accord with God's will and good pleasure — and so it seems to itself ready to do everything else except this: to be deprived of the thing it loves. The third, moreover, is ready even for this, if it so please God; and inquires only whether it does please him.

paras.la: Et sic patet totam hanc meditationem eo tendere, ut ostendat animae quam turpe et perversum sit, si non solum exuere nolit inordinatas cupiditates, sed si velit quidem eas exuere, sed eo modo velit quo ipsi libeat, et se non resignat in manibus Dei. Ex quo apparet illam esse voluntatem admodum debilem, quia vere vult et non vult.
paras.en: And so it is plain that this whole meditation tends to show the soul how base and perverse it is, not only to be unwilling to put off its inordinate desires, but even to be willing to put them off — yet in the manner that pleases itself, without resigning itself into the hands of God. From which it appears that such a will is a very feeble one, for in truth it wills and wills not.

paras.la: Unde, quia res haec tanti momenti est, praesertim ad disponendam animam electioni iam vicinae, posset etiam qui exercitia sumit, ad maiorem claritatem, praeter hanc similitudinem trium mercatorum, effingere sibi alias similitudines eiusdem tenoris: ut v. g. si essent tres aegroti, qui sanari quidem omnes cupiunt; sed primus nolit adhibere medicinas ullas propter earum amaritudinem, nec abscissionem propter dolorem; secundus velit quidem adhibere, sed quas ipse probet ac iudicet, non eas quae aptae sunt eius morbo — ut v. g. si nollet abstinere a vino, aut similibus; tertius denique se totum medico permittat, ut et dietam imperet, et urat, et secet ipsa etiam membra, si opus sit.
paras.en: Hence, since this matter is of such moment, especially for disposing the soul for the election now near at hand, the one taking the Exercises might also, for greater clarity, besides this similitude of the three merchants, fashion for himself other similitudes of the same tenor: as, for example, three sick men, all of whom indeed desire to be healed; but the first will not take any medicines because of their bitterness, nor suffer an incision because of the pain; the second is willing to take some, but only such as he himself approves and judges fit, not those suited to his disease — as, for instance, if he would not abstain from wine, or the like; the third, finally, gives himself over wholly to the physician, to prescribe his diet, to cauterize, and even to cut off his very limbs, if need be.

paras.rub: Quandonam electionem facturo proponendi tres gradus humilitatis
paras.la: Porro, simul cum his duabus meditationibus quas diximus — nempe de duobus vexillis et de tribus classibus — vel, si ita melius videatur, sequenti die, post meditationem de transitu Christi a Nazareth et de eius baptismo, proponuntur electionem facturo tres gradus humilitatis, ut, quemadmodum dicitur in libro exercitiorum, toto die eos animo verset; simul tamen unum vel duo mysteria vitae Christi eodem die, sicut in reliquis diebus, meditanda sunt. Nam hi tres gradus non dantur pro certa hora alicuius meditationis, cum non contineant nisi unum punctum praecipuum — scilicet desiderium attingendi tertium illum gradum humilitatis — quod toto die mente revolvendum est extra meditationem; immo etiam in meditatione opportuno tempore, adhibito triplici illo colloquio de vexillis, ut ibidem dicitur.
paras.en: Further, together with these two meditations we have mentioned — that of the Two Standards and that of the Three Classes — or, if it seems better, on the following day, after the meditation on Christ's journey from Nazareth and on his baptism, the three degrees of humility are proposed to the one about to make the election, so that, as is said in the book of the Exercises, he may turn them over in his mind the whole day; yet at the same time one or two mysteries of the life of Christ are to be meditated that day, as on the other days. For these three degrees are not given for a fixed hour of any meditation, since they contain but one chief point — namely, the desire of attaining that third degree of humility — which is to be revolved in the mind all day outside the meditation; indeed also within the meditation at a fitting time, using that triple colloquy of the Standards, as is said there.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXX
kapitel.la_titel: De ipsa electione iuxta rationem secundi temporis
kapitel.en_titel: On the election itself according to the manner of the second time

paras.la: His peractis, accedendum iam propius est ad electionem, et in primis declarandum praeludium electionum, quod fere coincidit cum fundamento posito ante exercitia; et ideo qui bene illud meditatus fuerit, nullam in hoc habebit difficultatem.
paras.en: These things done, one must now come closer to the election, and first of all explain the prelude of the elections, which almost coincides with the Foundation placed before the Exercises; and so whoever has meditated that well will have no difficulty here.

paras.la: Interim instructor exploret voluntatem exercentis se: an habeat indifferentiam, de cuius necessitate supra locuti sumus; et si magis propendere ad imperfectiorem statum animadverterit, explicet ei illud notabile quod est in exercitiis post tres classes: ut scilicet qui sentit affectum repugnantem paupertati reali, petat a Deo ut ipsum potius inclinet in illam partem. Cuius ratio est, quia virga incurva flectenda est in contrariam partem, ut deinde, manens in medio, fiat recta: quod praesertim locum habet in hac materia, cum illa pars sit securior, et hoc nihil impediat vel Dei voluntatem vel libertatem nostram. Hoc ergo supposito, pergendum est in meditationibus mysteriorum Christi quae sunt in libro exercitiorum, et simul vacandum electioni; ad quam dirigendam danda sunt tria illa tempora recte eligendi, voce vel scripto, ut magis videbitur instructori.
paras.en: Meanwhile let the instructor examine the will of the exercitant: whether he has the indifference of whose necessity we spoke above; and if he observes him leaning more toward the less perfect state, let him explain to him that note which stands in the Exercises after the Three Classes: namely, that whoever feels an affection repugnant to actual poverty should ask God rather to incline him toward that side. The reason for this is that a bent rod must be bowed to the contrary side, so that, coming to rest in the middle, it may become straight: which holds especially in this matter, since that side is the safer, and this in no way hinders either God's will or our freedom. This being supposed, one should proceed with the meditations on the mysteries of Christ which are in the book of the Exercises, and at the same time attend to the election; for the directing of which the three times of choosing rightly are to be given, by word or in writing, as shall seem better to the instructor.

paras.la: Electio autem ita peragenda est: non ut electurus meditetur tria illa tempora toto tempore meditationis, sed post peractam unamquamque meditationem, vel in aliqua eius parte, cum animus iam quietus est, tunc tempus proprium est agendi et ratiocinandi circa rem propositam. Et ideo diligenter curandum est ut meditationes, quemadmodum diximus, de Christi vita diligenter fiant suo tempore. Nam si quis, omissis suis meditationibus, vellet se totum dare cogitationi de electione status, non bene faceret, idque ei damnum afferret: quia per meditationes anima corroboratur et illuminatur et elevatur a terrenis, unde fit aptior ad Dei voluntatem et cognoscendam et amplectendam, et ad superanda omnia impedimenta; et contra, si cessaret a meditando, obscurior fieret et infirmior.
paras.en: The election is to be carried out thus: not that the one about to choose should meditate on those three times during the whole time of meditation; but after each meditation is finished, or in some part of it, when the mind is now quiet — that is the proper time for working and reasoning about the matter proposed. And therefore diligent care must be taken that the meditations on the life of Christ, as we have said, be diligently made at their own time. For if anyone, leaving aside his meditations, wished to give himself wholly to thinking about the election of a state, he would not do well, and it would bring him harm: because through the meditations the soul is strengthened and illumined and lifted from earthly things, whence it becomes more apt both to know and to embrace the will of God, and to overcome all hindrances; and on the contrary, if it ceased from meditating, it would become darker and weaker.
paras.note: Margin: 'Ex 3. tempore bonae electionis.'

paras.la: Quare, ut dictum est, dandum est suum tempus meditationi divinarum rerum, quae pro varietate mysteriorum occurrunt, et suum deinde tempus electioni: ne, si anima tota occupetur in hoc negocio, haec una cogitatio exsugat et exhauriat quodammodo succum et florem devotionis, et ita reddatur languidior.
paras.en: Therefore, as has been said, its own time is to be given to the meditation of divine things, which occur according to the variety of the mysteries, and its own time then to the election: lest, if the soul be wholly occupied in this business, this one thought suck out and drain, as it were, the sap and flower of devotion, and the soul thereby be made more languid.

paras.la: Quod si adhuc magis in particulari quaeratur quomodo hoc faciendum sit, dicendum: quod, si in secundo tempore eligendi versetur, debet qui deliberat, sine ulla sua ratiocinatione aut discursu adhibito, dum facit meditationem aut colloquia — et in summa dum constitutus est ante Deum — proponere oculis mentis suae viam consiliorum, et observare an sentiat in anima sua motus aliquos consolationis aut desolationis; deinde proponere sibi viam mandatorum, et hoc idem circa eam observare.
paras.en: If it is asked still more particularly how this is to be done, the answer is: if he is in the second time of choosing, the one deliberating should, without applying any reasoning or discourse of his own, while making the meditation or the colloquies — in short, while he stands before God — set before the eyes of his mind the way of the counsels, and observe whether he feels in his soul any motions of consolation or desolation; then set before himself the way of the commandments, and observe the same regarding it.

paras.la: Nec est ad hoc necessaria particularis meditatio, ut paulo ante dictum est, sed sufficit hoc facere dum versatur in meditationibus et orationibus consuetis. Et hoc idem faciat extra tempus meditationis, proponendo hoc modo dicto, et observando motus praedictos: nihil discurrendo per se, sed tantum audiendo vocem Domini, et se ad eam audiendam et ad motum illum accipiendum disponendo quantum poterit; maxime renovando saepe resignationem et desiderium cognoscendi divinum beneplacitum, et hoc semper curando: ut cesset omnis propria voluntas aut inclinatio.
paras.en: Nor is a special meditation necessary for this, as was said a little before; it is enough to do it while he is engaged in his customary meditations and prayers. And let him do the same outside the time of meditation, proposing the matter in the way described and observing the aforesaid motions: reasoning nothing by himself, but only listening for the voice of the Lord, and disposing himself as much as he can to hear it and to receive that motion — above all by often renewing his resignation and his desire of knowing the divine good pleasure, and by always taking care of this: that all his own will and inclination cease.

paras.la: Cum autem venerit instructor, exigat ab eo rationem huiusmodi motionum; et si boni vel mali spiritus signa deprehendat, utatur regulis de discernendis spiritibus — sed iis praecipue quae secundae hebdomadae conveniunt — et declaret ei quantum satis esse iudicabit ad ipsum dirigendum, vel erigendum si opus fuerit. Et si bene procedere hac via videbit, alia meditatione proposita, hortetur ut eandem viam teneat circa electionem propositam, ut experiatur an durent eaedem motiones, an aliae contrariae succedant; quod si contrariae occurrerint, conetur discernere per praedictas regulas quae sint bonae, quae malae.
paras.en: When the instructor comes, let him require of him an account of these motions; and if he detects signs of the good or the evil spirit, let him use the Rules for the Discernment of Spirits — but chiefly those belonging to the Second Week — and explain to him as much as he shall judge sufficient for directing him, or for raising him up if need be. And if he sees that he is proceeding well by this way, when another meditation has been proposed, let him exhort him to keep the same way with regard to the proposed election, to test whether the same motions last, or others contrary to them follow; and if contrary ones occur, let him try to discern by the aforesaid rules which are good and which bad.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXI
kapitel.la_titel: De electione iuxta priorem et posteriorem modum
kapitel.en_titel: On the election according to the first and the second way

paras.rub: Quid, si hoc tempore non conficitur electio
paras.la: Si hoc secundo tempore non conficitur electio — quia qui exercetur nullam notatu dignam motionem in se sentit, vel sentit in utramque partem — adhibendi sunt modi tertii temporis, prior et posterior, qui ei declarandi erunt: ut, cum priori modo aliquid constituerit, idem deinde expendat posteriori; et si idem resultet ex utroque, id bonum signum est bonae electionis.
paras.en: If in this second time the election is not accomplished — because the exercitant feels in himself no motion worth noting, or feels them toward both sides — the ways of the third time, the first and the second, are to be employed, and are to be explained to him: so that, when he has settled something by the first way, he then weigh the same by the second; and if the same result comes from both, that is a good sign of a good election.

paras.la: Hoc autem tertio tempore poterit dari una tantum meditatio ex iis quae secunda hebdomada proponuntur, cum sua repetitione, ut reliquum tempus impendatur electioni; idque videtur innui in libro exercitiorum per exemplum contemplationis baptismi, quae ponitur quinta die. Quanquam, cum hoc non praecipiatur, credi potest quod permittitur instructori, ut unam vel duas in die det meditationes, ut viderit exercitanti magis profuturum, pro difficultate quam sentiat, et prout indigeat tempore ad faciendam hanc discussionem.
paras.en: In this third time only one meditation of those proposed in the Second Week may be given, with its repetition, so that the remaining time may be spent on the election; and this seems to be hinted in the book of the Exercises by the example of the contemplation of the Baptism, which is placed on the fifth day. Yet since this is not commanded, it may be believed that it is left to the instructor to give one or two meditations a day, as he shall see to be more profitable to the exercitant, according to the difficulty he feels, and as he needs time for making this examination.

paras.la: Monendus etiam erit ut notet scripto rationes quae se offerunt pro utraque parte, idque seorsim: nam rationes omnes cuiusque partis simul collectae magis veritatem ostendunt, et maiorem vim habent ad movendum. Has vero cum instructore conferre debebit, ut ab eo melius dirigi possit.
paras.en: He should also be advised to note down in writing the reasons that present themselves for each side, and that separately: for all the reasons of each side, gathered together, show the truth better and have greater force to move. And these he should confer with the instructor, that he may be the better directed by him.

paras.la: Porro illud etiam cavendum instructori: ne in hoc negocio, per se tam difficili et laborioso, nimis obruat exercitantem, nec semper eum stimulet et fatiget; quin potius sinendus est aliquando respirare, ne semper affligatur, aut absorbeatur tristitia aut taedio, et desperatione abiiciat seipsum — quod tunc maxime metuendum est, cum praeter propriam infirmitatem et repugnantiam carnis accedunt etiam daemonum impugnationes. Difficile est enim relevare eiusmodi cor, cum semel conciderit.
paras.en: Further, the instructor must also beware of this: not to overwhelm the exercitant too much in this business, so difficult and laborious in itself, nor to be always spurring and wearying him; rather he should sometimes be allowed to breathe, lest he be continually afflicted, or swallowed up by sadness or weariness, and cast himself down in despair — which is most to be feared when, besides his own weakness and the resistance of the flesh, the assaults of the demons are added as well. For it is hard to raise up such a heart once it has fallen.

paras.rub: Ut sustinendus qui non prompte respondet vocationi divinae
paras.la: Immo vero, etiam si quis cerneretur minus prompte respondere divinae voluntati, nec se vincere ut deberet, sustinendus tamen patienter esset, et expectandum ut paulatim et quasi pedetentim superet obices illi oppositos; et in hoc etiam imitandus mos divinae bonitatis, cui cooperamur: quae omnia suaviter disponit, et longanimiter expectat animae moras in veniendo ad eum.
paras.en: Indeed, even if someone were seen to respond less promptly to the divine will, and not to conquer himself as he ought, he should nevertheless be borne with patiently, and one should wait for him to overcome, little by little and as it were step by step, the obstacles set against him; and in this too the manner of the divine goodness, with which we cooperate, is to be imitated: which disposes all things sweetly, and waits long-sufferingly upon the soul's delays in coming to him.

paras.la: Denique hoc etiam advertendum: quicquid eliget secundo vel tertio tempore, ne votum ullum emittat, ut dicitur annotatione decimaquarta — et praesertim in secundo tempore. Saepe enim in illo calore vel consolatione fiunt vota, quae deinde displicent; et hoc praesertim servandum cum iis qui natura sunt ferventi et praecipiti, vel parum stabili. Sed tamen, si electio facta esset maturo consilio, ut cum magna claritate et indiciis haud obscuris divinae vocationis — praesertim si aetas aut natura hominis non esset suspecta — et hic suam electionem voto firmare cuperet, ut se melius muniret contra oppugnationes carnis et mundi et satanae, non potest instructor, nec debet, eius devotionem impedire, sicut nec ad id ulla ratione impellere.
paras.en: Finally, this too is to be observed: whatever he shall choose in the second or third time, let him make no vow, as is said in the fourteenth Annotation — and especially in the second time. For often in that heat, or consolation, vows are made which afterwards displease; and this is to be kept above all with those who are by nature fervent and precipitate, or little stable. Yet if the election had been made with mature counsel, with great clarity and with signs by no means obscure of the divine vocation — especially if the age or the character of the man gave no ground for suspicion — and he desired to confirm his election with a vow, in order to arm himself better against the assaults of the flesh, the world and Satan, the instructor cannot and ought not hinder his devotion, just as he ought not by any means urge him to it.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXII
kapitel.la_titel: De oratione post factam electionem
kapitel.en_titel: On prayer after the election has been made

paras.la: Ultimum est in hac electione id quod in libello exercitiorum ponitur in ultimo puncto: ut homo post conclusam electionem ad orationem se conferat. Quo tempore, si senserit mentem suam confirmari in electione iam facta, sentiendo in se motiones aliquas vel illustrationes desuper immissas — ita ut Deus approbare videatur quod factum est, et promittere vires ad exequendum — id est optimum indicium, et haberi debet tanquam sigillum totius electionis.
paras.en: The last thing in this election is what is set down in the little book of the Exercises in the final point: that after the election is concluded a man betake himself to prayer. If at that time he feels his mind confirmed in the election now made, sensing in himself certain motions or illuminations sent from above — so that God seems to approve what has been done, and to promise strength to carry it out — that is the best sign, and is to be held as the seal of the whole election.

paras.rub: Quid, cum electio a malo spiritu tentatur
paras.la: Si vero motiones, vel affectus, vel illustrationes intellectus eiusmodi essent quae infirmarent electionem factam, et, examinatae iuxta regulas supra positas, viderentur a malo spiritu, vel saltem essent dubiae, non est mutanda electio.
paras.en: But if the motions, or affections, or illuminations of the understanding were such as to weaken the election made, and, examined by the rules set down above, appeared to be from the evil spirit, or at least were doubtful, the election is not to be changed.

paras.rub: Quid, si sit a bono spiritu
paras.la: Si autem clare appareret esse a bono spiritu, signum est discursum non fuisse bonum, et electionem denuo faciendam.
paras.en: If, however, it should clearly appear to be from the good spirit, it is a sign that the reasoning was not good, and that the election is to be made anew.

paras.rub: Quid, si in oratione nihil notabile acciderit
paras.la: Quod si in hac oratione nihil in utramvis partem notabile accideret, nec in affectu nec in intellectu, et voluntas eligentis in suo proposito perseverat, non est electio in dubium revocanda; sed ita putandum est: voluisse Deum per discursum rationis voluntatem suam inveniri.
paras.en: But if in this prayer nothing notable should happen toward either side, neither in the affections nor in the understanding, and the will of the chooser perseveres in its purpose, the election is not to be called into doubt; rather it is to be thought that God willed his will to be found through the discourse of reason.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXIII
kapitel.la_titel: Quid agendum instructori, cum sentit eum qui electionem facit hallucinari
kapitel.en_titel: What the instructor should do when he perceives that the one making the election is deceiving himself

paras.la: Caeterum illud quoque interdum contingere solet: ut exercitia sumens hallucinetur in electione facienda, et, licet Deus illum vocet ad vitam perfectiorem, ipse tamen — vel propter daemonis deceptionem, vel propter propriam infirmitatem — imperfectiorem eligat, idque a Spiritu Sancto esse putet, nec ab eo dimoveri possit.
paras.en: It also sometimes happens that the one taking the Exercises deceives himself in making the election, and, although God calls him to the more perfect life, he nevertheless — whether through the deception of the demon or through his own weakness — chooses the less perfect, and thinks this to be from the Holy Spirit, and cannot be moved from it.

paras.la: Tunc igitur prudentiae est ut instructor non multum reluctetur — quod frustra faceret — sed neque ex altera parte confirmet electionem factam; ac potius ostendat sibi non valde satisfecisse, sed sperare quod progressu temporis Dominus ei clarius indicabit voluntatem suam. Et sic eum relinquat aliquantum dubium et incertum de tali electione; deinde etiam instruat quomodo disponere se debeat, ne aditum claudat divinae luci.
paras.en: In that case it is the part of prudence that the instructor not resist much — which he would do in vain — but neither, on the other hand, confirm the election made; rather let him show that it has not greatly satisfied him, but that he hopes that with the passage of time the Lord will indicate his will to him more clearly. And so let him leave him somewhat doubtful and uncertain about that election; and then also instruct him how he ought to dispose himself, so as not to shut the entrance to the divine light.

paras.la: Saepe enim experientia monstravit quosdam, qui in ipso conflictu exercitiorum succubuerant, deinde extra exercitia commodius veritatem agnovisse, idque ex iisdem principiis quae hauserant in ipsis exercitiis: sive quia daemon acrius oppugnat in illo articulo electionis; sive quod natura ipsa, praesertim in iis qui timidiores sunt et pusillanimes, in illa quasi agonia quodammodo opprimitur et suffocatur — ita cum deinde quodammodo respirat, est melius disposita ad ratiocinandum et percipiendum lumen Dei; sive denique quia experientia deinde cognoverunt se non eam vitam posse in saeculo tenere, quam fortasse in exercitiis vel ipsi sibi finxerant, vel eis daemon persuaserat.
paras.en: For experience has often shown that some who had succumbed in the very conflict of the Exercises afterwards, outside the Exercises, recognized the truth more readily — and that from the same principles they had drawn in the Exercises themselves: whether because the demon attacks more fiercely at that moment of the election; or because nature itself, especially in those who are more timid and faint-hearted, is in that agony, as it were, in some measure oppressed and stifled — so that when it afterwards breathes again, it is better disposed for reasoning and for perceiving the light of God; or, finally, because they afterwards learned by experience that they could not maintain in the world the kind of life which perhaps, during the Exercises, they had either imagined for themselves or the demon had persuaded them of.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXIV
kapitel.la_titel: De iis qui iam statum habent
kapitel.en_titel: On those who already have a state of life

paras.la: Post tractationem de electione ponitur a nostro Patre methodus quaedam de emendatione seu reformatione vitae: quae doctrina maximi momenti est pro iis qui iam sunt in statu immutabili, vel saltem quos Deus non vocat ad mutationem status. Per hanc enim reformationem tolluntur multi abusus, qui, etiamsi non sint peccata, saltem sunt origo multorum malorum.
paras.en: After the treatment of the election, Our Father sets down a certain method for the amendment, or reformation, of life: a teaching of the greatest moment for those who are already in an unchangeable state, or at least whom God does not call to a change of state. For by this reformation many abuses are removed which, even if they are not sins, are at least the origin of many evils.

paras.la: Hac vero doctrina id agitur: ut multi qui iam uxorem et familiam habent, licet in saeculo maneant, suo tamen modo perfectionem sectentur — ad quam nos quoque invitare et perducere eos debemus ex vocatione nostra, itaque passim iubent Constitutiones nostrae. Nec est dubium quin, si proximos iuvare conaremur ac dirigere ad hanc formulam quae hic expressa est, valde insignis fructus sequeretur. Itaque hoc omnibus operariis Societatis valde commendatum esse deberet.
paras.en: What this teaching aims at is that many who already have a wife and household, though they remain in the world, may yet in their own way pursue perfection — to which we too, by our vocation, ought to invite and lead them, as our Constitutions everywhere enjoin. Nor is there any doubt that if we strove to help our neighbours and direct them by this formula set out here, a very notable fruit would follow. This, therefore, ought to be much commended to all the workers of the Society.

paras.rub: Quis modus tenendus in iuvandis habentibus firmum statum
paras.la: Cum his igitur hunc modum tenere oportet: ut praeter exercitia ordinaria de mysteriis vitae Christi dentur etiam illa de duobus vexillis et tribus hominum classibus, immo etiam praeludium electionum. Haec enim, licet non adeo necessaria sint ut iis qui de toto vitae statu deliberaturi sunt, non potest tamen dubitari quin valde sint utilia, ut animentur ad eam perfectionem cuius ipsorum saltem status ac conditio est capax.
paras.en: With these persons, then, this manner is to be kept: besides the ordinary exercises on the mysteries of the life of Christ, those on the Two Standards and the Three Classes of Men should also be given, and indeed the prelude of the elections as well. For although these are not so necessary as for those who are to deliberate about their whole state of life, it cannot be doubted that they are very useful for encouraging them toward that perfection of which their state and condition, at least, is capable.

paras.la: Caeterum secundus modus eligendi non valde ad hoc negocium pertinet, sed potius tertius modus, eiusque membrum utrumque. Res autem instituenda ita est, ut singula puncta discutiantur — v. g. de familia, vel de expensis — et, post deliberationem factam de uno puncto, transeatur ad aliud; in singulis autem maius vel minus tempus insumatur, ut fuerit negocii gravitas vel difficultas. Aliquando enim una hora, aut etiam plures, in uno puncto insumendae erunt; aliquando autem plura puncta in una hora concludentur.
paras.en: For the rest, the second manner of choosing does not much pertain to this business, but rather the third manner, and both its members. The matter should be so arranged that the several points are examined one by one — for example, concerning the household, or expenses — and, when the deliberation on one point is finished, one passes to another; and on each, more or less time is to be spent according to the weight or difficulty of the business. Sometimes one hour, or even several, will have to be spent on a single point; at other times several points will be concluded in one hour.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXV
kapitel.la_titel: De tertia hebdomada
kapitel.en_titel: On the Third Week

paras.rub: In tertia hebdomada stabilitur vitae melioris electio
paras.la: In tertia hebdomada stabilitur et confirmatur electio vitae melioris iam facta, et voluntas serviendi Deo, proposito tanto et tali exemplo: nempe passione Domini et Salvatoris nostri. In ea enim omnes eius virtutes multo insignius atque excellentius elucent, et efficacius nos invitant ad sui imitationem. Itaque magnus hic thesaurus reconditus est; unde videmus sanctos omnes in hac potissimum parte se exercuisse, ut apparet ex libris quos scriptos reliquerunt. Et ideo in hoc etiam oportet meditantem diligenter instrui, quoniam hic esse deberet ordinarius animae cibus.
paras.en: In the Third Week the election of a better life already made is established and confirmed, together with the will to serve God, by the setting forth of so great and such an example: namely, the Passion of our Lord and Saviour. For in it all his virtues shine forth far more notably and excellently, and invite us more effectively to their imitation. A great treasure, then, lies hidden here; whence we see that all the saints exercised themselves above all in this part, as appears from the books they left in writing. And therefore in this too the one meditating must be carefully instructed, since this ought to be the soul's ordinary food.

paras.rub: Idem ordo harum meditationum ut in secunda hebdomada
paras.la: Ordo et discursus harum meditationum est idem qui in praeterita hebdomada: nempe intuendo personas, dicta et opera. Debet tamen, iis praesertim qui non adeo sunt exercitati, aperiri via in hac materia per illa puncta quae communiter tradi solent: quis patiatur, quid patiatur, a quibus, et propter quos.
paras.en: The order and course of these meditations is the same as in the preceding Week: namely, by looking upon the persons, the words and the deeds. Yet, especially for those not so practised, a way should be opened into this matter through the points commonly taught: who suffers, what he suffers, at whose hands, and for whose sake.

paras.rub: Quomodo in compositione loci quis se statuat
paras.la: In compositione loci debet qui meditatur ita se constituere, quasi praesens esset mysterio illi dum ageretur — et quidem ac si gestum esset propter se solum, iuxta formam illam Apostoli: Qui dilexit me, et tradidit semetipsum pro me. Itaque debet anima ita se respicere, quasi ipsa causa fuerit tantorum dolorum et ignominiarum quas Dei Filius perpessus est; deinde videre quidquid bonorum spiritualium, quidquid gratiae — et quod ab aeternis malis liberata sit, quod aeterna bona se consecuturam speret — haec omnia ex Christi meritis sibi provenisse. Immo etiam considerare Christum, dum illa pateretur, habuisse ante oculos et nos et nostra peccata in particulari omnia, et pro iis orasse, eorumque remissionem et gratiam nobis impetrasse.
paras.en: In the composition of place, the one meditating should so place himself as if he were present at that mystery while it was happening — and indeed as if it had been done for him alone, after that pattern of the Apostle: Who loved me, and gave himself up for me. The soul, then, should so regard itself as though it had itself been the cause of the great sorrows and ignominies which the Son of God endured; and then see that whatever spiritual goods, whatever grace it has — its deliverance from eternal evils, its hope of attaining eternal goods — all this has come to it from the merits of Christ. Nay more, it should consider that Christ, while he suffered those things, had before his eyes both us and all our sins in particular, and prayed for them, and obtained for us their forgiveness and grace.

paras.la: Quamquam autem affectus compassionis est valde bonus, debetque et peti cum instantia, et desiderari cum humilitate, et excipi cum gratia, debent tamen simul etiam curari alii affectus, qui sunt utiliores ad profectum nostrum spiritualem.
paras.en: Now although the affection of compassion is very good, and should be asked for with insistence, desired with humility, and received with thanksgiving, yet at the same time other affections should also be cultivated, which are more useful for our spiritual progress.

paras.la: Primus autem est: quanta res sit offendere Deum, quando ad satisfaciendum ei divina sapientia dignum putavit adhibere ipsum Filii sui sanguinem et vitam. Ex quo etiam nascitur summum odium peccati, quod praesertim ab illa iustitia tam severis poenis vindicetur: quia si hoc in viridi, quid in arido?
paras.en: The first is: how great a thing it is to offend God, seeing that, to make satisfaction to him, the divine wisdom thought it fitting to employ the very blood and life of his Son. From this too is born a supreme hatred of sin, seeing above all that that justice avenges it with such severe penalties: for if this is done in the green wood, what shall be done in the dry?

paras.la: Secundo, cognoscenda et veneranda est bonitas et sapientia Dei infinita, quae tam aptum medium invenit, ut hominum corda amore suo liquefacta ad se attraheret; iuxta Apostolum: Commendat Deus charitatem suam in nobis, quoniam cum inimici essemus, etc. (Rom. 5, 8).
paras.en: Second, the infinite goodness and wisdom of God is to be known and venerated, which found so apt a means to draw men's hearts to himself, melted by his love; according to the Apostle: God commends his charity toward us, in that while we were yet enemies, etc. (Rom 5:8).

paras.la: Tertio, hic etiam confirmatur spes nostra: quia, ut ait S. Augustinus, qui dedit quod plus est — nempe unigeniti sui sanguinem — dabit et gloriam aeternam, quae minus est sine dubio. Et ideo hic Christi sanguis tenendus est ut arrha et pignus tum divini amoris, tum futurae beatitudinis.
paras.en: Third, here our hope also is confirmed: for, as St. Augustine says, he who gave the greater thing — the blood of his only-begotten Son — will give eternal glory too, which is without doubt the lesser. And therefore this blood of Christ is to be held as the earnest and pledge both of the divine love and of the blessedness to come.

paras.la: Quarto — et omnium maxime — inflammatur amor in Deum, consideratione tantae bonitatis et tanti beneficii nobis dati, et dati tali modo.
paras.en: Fourth — and most of all — love toward God is inflamed by the consideration of such great goodness, and of so great a benefit given to us, and given in such a manner.

paras.la: Quinto, sic etiam animantur omnes ad perfectam imitationem, ut ait S. Petrus: Christus passus est pro nobis, vobis relinquens exemplum, ut sequamini vestigia eius (1 Petr. 2, 21). Turpe enim esset et intolerabile, cum ille, ut nos pro nostra ipsorum salute doceret, non dedignatus sit tam humilia perpeti, si nos, quorum salus agitur, recusemus.
paras.en: Fifth, all are thus also spurred to perfect imitation, as St. Peter says: Christ suffered for us, leaving you an example, that you should follow his footsteps (1 Pet 2:21). For it would be shameful and intolerable if, when he — to teach us, for the sake of our own salvation — did not disdain to endure things so lowly, we, whose salvation is at stake, should refuse.

paras.la: Denique potest etiam et debet concipi magnus zelus animarum: quas videlicet Deus tanti aestimavit, et tanto affectu amavit, et tam magno pretio emit.
paras.en: Finally, a great zeal for souls can and should also be conceived: souls which God so highly esteemed, loved with so great an affection, and bought at so great a price.

paras.la: Iuvat etiam habere in promptu hac hebdomada aliquas sententias sacrae Scripturae ad Domini passionem pertinentes: ex psalmis, vel ex prophetis — et maxime ex Isaia — vel etiam ex Evangeliis, aut ex epistolis Pauli; quae vel magnitudinem dolorum ac cruciatuum Christi Domini indicent, vel eius bonitatem, aut effectus mirabiles in hominum reparatione. Quae extra meditationem valde proderunt ad cor excitandum, et etiam ad tollendam nescio quam satietatem, quae subrepere solet ex continuatione earundem rerum. Haec autem loca Scripturae poterit instructor colligere, vel ab alio iam collecta suppeditare: sunt enim multa, et passim occurrunt.
paras.en: It is also helpful in this Week to have at hand some sentences of holy Scripture bearing on the Lord's Passion: from the Psalms, or from the Prophets — above all from Isaiah — or also from the Gospels or the epistles of Paul; such as show either the greatness of the sorrows and torments of Christ the Lord, or his goodness, or the wonderful effects in the restoration of mankind. Outside the meditation these will be of great profit for stirring the heart, and also for removing a certain satiety which tends to creep in from the continuation of the same matters. These passages of Scripture the instructor can gather himself, or supply from another's existing collection: for they are many, and occur everywhere.

paras.rub: Caetera quaerenda ex libello exercitiorum; regulae victus
paras.la: Cetera quae ad hanc hebdomadam pertinent scripta sunt in libro exercitiorum clare et distincte, in meditationibus et additionibus. In particulari autem, quae in fine huius hebdomadae traduntur de regulis ad victum temperandum, non est quod scripta dentur, sed verbo tantum explicentur: tum ob alias causas, tum quia non omnibus eodem modo proponendae sunt, sed adhibita discretione, pro cuiusque complexione et viribus tam corporis quam animi.
paras.en: The rest of what belongs to this Week is written clearly and distinctly in the book of the Exercises, in the meditations and Additions. In particular, the rules given at the end of this Week for the ordering of one's food need not be given in writing, but only explained by word of mouth: both for other reasons, and because they are not to be proposed to all in the same way, but with discretion, according to each one's constitution and the strength both of body and of soul.

paras.la: Notandum etiam quod hae regulae non solum proponi debent hac hebdomada, sed antea etiam aliquo opportuno tempore; saltem, si tamen prius factum non est, hic declarentur. Fortasse enim in hunc locum dilatae sunt, ne prioribus hebdomadis nimis oneraretur is qui in exercitiis versatur tot documentis extra ipsas meditationes. In hac autem hebdomada multo pauciora sunt eiusmodi documenta, et sic magis vacabit instructori ea explicare. Expedit enim ut semper aliquid novi afferat, cum illum cui tradit exercitia invisit.
paras.en: It should also be noted that these rules should be proposed not only in this Week, but earlier as well, at some opportune time; at least, if it has not been done before, let them be explained here. Perhaps they were deferred to this place lest, in the earlier Weeks, the one engaged in the Exercises be too much burdened with so many instructions outside the meditations themselves. In this Week, however, such instructions are far fewer, and so the instructor will have more leisure to explain them. For it is expedient that he always bring something new when he visits the one to whom he is giving the Exercises.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXVI
kapitel.la_titel: De quarta hebdomada
kapitel.en_titel: On the Fourth Week

paras.la: Quarta hebdomada videtur respondere viae unitivae: tota enim exercetur in amore Dei et desiderio aeternitatis, cuius tanquam exemplar proponitur resurrectio Christi, eaque gaudia quae etiam in hoc mundo eam consecuta sunt. Possent etiam hic addi aliquae meditationes de gloria Paradisi, et de futura iustorum felicitate, cuius pignus accepimus in hoc mysterio resurrectionis Christi: quia, iuxta Apostolum, Deus nos etiam conresuscitavit, et considere fecit cum illo (Ephes. 2, 6). Quare eo magis excitari debemus ad contemnenda terrena et caelestia appetenda, iuxta illud eiusdem: Si consurrexistis cum Christo, quae sursum sunt quaerite, quae sursum sunt sapite, etc. (Coloss. 3, 1).
paras.en: The Fourth Week seems to correspond to the unitive way: for it is wholly exercised in the love of God and the desire of eternity, of which the Resurrection of Christ is set forth as the exemplar, together with those joys which followed it even in this world. Here might also be added some meditations on the glory of Paradise and on the future happiness of the just, the pledge of which we have received in this mystery of Christ's Resurrection: for, according to the Apostle, God has also raised us up together with him, and made us sit together with him (Eph 2:6). Wherefore we ought to be the more stirred to despise earthly things and desire heavenly ones, according to the same Apostle's word: If you have risen with Christ, seek the things that are above; mind the things that are above, etc. (Col 3:1).

paras.la: Exercitium de amore Dei est valde aptum ad amorem nostrum in Deum excitandum, et continet quattuor puncta foecundissima, et quae magnam materiam suppeditant ad meditandum. Potest autem duobus modis fieri. Primo, iisdem diebus cum aliis mysteriis resurrectionis: ita ut secundo die, postquam coepta sint mysteria resurrectionis, incipiatur etiam haec meditatio de amando Deo, eique quotidie una aut altera hora tribuatur, distincta a meditatione illorum mysteriorum. Alter modus est, ut absolvantur prius omnia illa mysteria, et deinde integer dies, aut duo dies, huic uni meditationi assignentur.
paras.en: The exercise on the love of God is very apt for stirring up our love toward God, and contains four most fruitful points, which supply great matter for meditation. It can be made in two ways. First, on the same days as the other mysteries of the Resurrection: so that on the second day after the mysteries of the Resurrection have been begun, this meditation on loving God is also begun, and one hour or two is given to it daily, distinct from the meditation on those mysteries. The other way is that all those mysteries be finished first, and then a whole day, or two days, be assigned to this one meditation.
paras.note: The 'exercise on the love of God' is the Contemplatio ad amorem (Contemplation to Attain Love) of the Exercises.

paras.la: Est autem bene notandum, et declarandum hanc meditationem aggredienti, quod in ea dicitur: amorem magis pendere ex operibus quam ex verbis, et consistere in mutua quadam facultatum et omnium rerum communicatione. Per hoc enim intelligere debet non sufficere sibi teneriorem quendam affectum quem in se sentiat, neque eo contentum esse debere. Verum est enim quod ait S. Gregorius: Probatio amoris exhibitio est operis; et amor, ubi est, magna operatur, et ubi operari renuit, amor non est. Nec aliud occurrit circa hanc quartam hebdomadam.
paras.en: It should be well noted, and explained to the one entering upon this meditation, what is said in it: that love depends more on deeds than on words, and consists in a certain mutual communication of goods and of all things. By this he must understand that a certain tender affection which he feels in himself is not enough for him, and that he ought not to rest content with it. For what St. Gregory says is true: The proof of love is the showing of the deed; and love, where it is, works great things, and where it refuses to work, it is not love. Nothing further occurs concerning this Fourth Week.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXVII
kapitel.la_titel: De tribus modis orandi
kapitel.en_titel: On the three methods of prayer

paras.la: Post exercitia adduntur aliqua documenta aptissima et valde utilia profectui spirituali. Primo autem loco ponuntur tres modi orandi: non ut omnes qui iam exercitia peregerint in eis exerceantur — nam hoc non necessarium est — sed ponuntur ad complementum doctrinae, et propter rudiores et minus capaces, qui scilicet non ita possunt habere perpetuos discursus in oratione, ut diutius haereant in una materia. Unde in Constitutionibus, parte 7, cap. 4, lit. F, dicitur exercitia plena non nisi paucis, primam hebdomadam cum his tribus modis orandi pluribus communicari posse.
paras.en: After the Exercises certain instructions are added, most apt and very useful for spiritual progress. In the first place are set the three methods of prayer: not that all who have already made the Exercises should practise them — for this is not necessary — but they are given for the completion of the teaching, and for the simpler and less capable, who cannot sustain continuous discourse in prayer so as to dwell long on one matter. Hence in the Constitutions, Part 7, chapter 4, letter F, it is said that the full Exercises can be given only to a few, while the First Week with these three methods of prayer can be communicated to more.

paras.rub: Primus modus: discurrere circa praecepta Dei etc.
paras.la: Primus ergo modus est discurrendo circa praecepta Dei aut Ecclesiae, et circa septem peccata capitalia, et tres potentias animae, et quinque sensus; et hoc non tam speculative quam practice: v. g. cogitando in praeceptis quomodo male ea servaverit, et proponendo in posterum melius servare; et sic de reliquis.
paras.en: The first method, then, is by discoursing on the commandments of God or of the Church, on the seven capital sins, the three powers of the soul, and the five senses; and this not so much speculatively as practically: for example, considering, as to the commandments, how badly he has kept them, and resolving to keep them better for the future; and so of the rest.

paras.la: Si vero hae materiae paulo altius elevandae essent, et exercitans capacior esset, hic modus praescribi posset. In praeceptis consideretur primo praeceptum ipsum in se, quam sit bonum et iustum et sanctum; secundo, quam utilis eius observantia; tertio, quomodo antea observatum sit — et si bene sit observatum, agendo gratias Deo; sin contra, dolendo et petendo veniam; quarto, proponendo in posterum perfectam et exactam observantiam, et petendo ad hoc gratiam per colloquium. Quo finito, si non expleta sit hora, transeatur ad aliud praeceptum eodem ordine.
paras.en: But if these matters were to be raised a little higher, and the exercitant were more capable, this method could be prescribed. Regarding the commandments, let him consider first the commandment itself in itself — how good and just and holy it is; second, how profitable its observance; third, how it has been kept hitherto — and if it has been kept well, giving thanks to God; if not, grieving and asking pardon; fourth, resolving upon perfect and exact observance for the future, and asking grace for this in a colloquy. This done, if the hour is not yet filled, let him pass to another commandment in the same order.

paras.la: In peccatis: primo videndo singula, quam mala sint et quam iuste prohibita; secundo, quantum noceant si non fugiantur; tertio, quomodo adhuc fugerit, vel in posterum decreverit fugere.
paras.en: Regarding the sins: first, seeing of each how evil it is and how justly forbidden; second, how much they harm if they are not fled; third, how he has fled them hitherto, or has resolved to flee them for the future.

paras.la: In potentiis et sensibus cogitari potest primo, quam nobiles et quam nobis utiles sint singulae — ut v. g. intellectus, et deinceps aliae; secundo, ad quem finem datae; tertio, quomodo iis usus sit Christus, vel Beatissima Virgo; quarto, quomodo nos usi simus, et dolendo quod male, etc. Et idem de aliis potentiis et sensibus sigillatim, et inter alia etiam de facultate loquendi, de virtute motiva, et similibus.
paras.en: Regarding the powers and senses one may consider first, how noble each is and how useful to us — as, for example, the understanding, and then the others; second, for what end they were given; third, how Christ used them, or the most Blessed Virgin; fourth, how we have used them, grieving that it was badly, and so on. And the same of the other powers and senses one by one — among others also of the faculty of speech, the power of movement, and the like.

paras.la: Est tamen advertendum: dum cogitamus quomodo usi simus his potentiis, vel, in meditandis praeceptis, quam male ea servaverimus — et maxime in meditandis peccatis — non ita debere institui meditationem, quasi examinare velimus conscientiam, ut fit cum nos praeparamus ad confessionem, vel etiam velimus de industria elicere contritionem: hoc enim pertinet ad primam hebdomadam. Sed hic principalis intentio est cogitare ipsas materias; ex occasione autem fit reflexio ad nos ipsos, et ideo in generali tantum debet fieri haec reflexio, non multum descendendo ad particularia peccata.
paras.en: It should, however, be observed that while we consider how we have used these powers, or, in meditating on the commandments, how badly we have kept them — and above all in meditating on the sins — the meditation is not to be so conducted as though we wished to examine our conscience, as is done when we prepare for confession, or as though we deliberately wished to elicit contrition: for that belongs to the First Week. Here the principal intention is to think on the matters themselves; the reflection upon ourselves arises by occasion, and therefore this reflection should be made only in general, without descending much to particular sins.

paras.rub: Hoc genus orandi a S. Xaverio commendatum
paras.la: Hoc orandi genus dicitur P. Franciscus Xaverius commendare solitus omnibus animabus quas tractabat, ita ut etiam poenitentiae loco iniungere soleret, ut mane et vespere aliquod tempus huic impenderent.
paras.en: Father Francis Xavier is said to have been wont to commend this kind of prayer to all the souls he dealt with — so much so that he would even enjoin it in place of a penance, that they spend some time on it morning and evening.

paras.la: Quamvis autem in libro exercitiorum dicatur tanto spatio esse immorandum quo oratio dominica ter recitari possit, tamen si quis in aliquo gustum inveniret, vel utilitatem aliquam spiritualem, deberet ibi haerere diutius, etiam si non posset absolvere omnia praecepta: iuxta id quod dicitur in quarta additione ad finem primae hebdomadae.
paras.en: Although it is said in the book of the Exercises that one should linger for the space in which the Lord's Prayer can be recited three times, yet if anyone should find relish in some point, or some spiritual profit, he ought to dwell there longer, even if he could not finish all the commandments: according to what is said in the fourth Addition at the end of the First Week.

paras.rub: Quid in secundo modo orandi notandum
paras.la: In secundo modo orandi notandum est: cum una vox non facit sensum, plures debere coniungi, ut Qui es in caelis, aut Sanctificetur nomen tuum. Aliae sunt voces quae solae praebent materiam meditationis, ut Pater, vel Noster.
paras.en: In the second method of prayer it should be noted that when one word does not yield a sense, several should be joined together, as Who art in heaven, or Hallowed be thy name. Other words by themselves afford matter for meditation, as Father, or Our.

paras.la: Quod autem hic dicitur de his orationibus, idem intelligendum est de aliquibus scripturae locis, ac praesertim psalmis: e quibus aliqui eligi possunt, vel psalmi toti, vel eorum versiculi, qui uberrime pascunt et intellectum et affectum.
paras.en: What is said here of these prayers is to be understood likewise of certain passages of Scripture, and especially of the Psalms: from which some may be chosen — whole psalms, or verses of them — which feed both the understanding and the affections most richly.

paras.la: Notandum est etiam: cum qui facit exercitia bene procedit in hoc orandi modo, ita ut eum satis tenere videatur, non esse necessarium ut multum in eo procedat, quia sufficit ut didicerit modum, quo deinde in posterum uti sciat. Quod idem intelligendum est de primo modo — nisi quod, cum ille habeat aliquanto maiorem varietatem, utile erit ut faciat unum exercitium circa praecepta, aliud circa peccata, aliud circa potentias animae, aliud circa sensus, etc.
paras.en: It should also be noted that when the one making the Exercises proceeds well in this method of prayer, so that he seems to grasp it sufficiently, it is not necessary for him to go far in it: it is enough that he has learned the method, so as to know how to use it thereafter. The same is to be understood of the first method — except that, since it has somewhat greater variety, it will be useful to make one exercise on the commandments, another on the sins, another on the powers of the soul, another on the senses, and so forth.

paras.la: Tertius modus orandi ita intelligendus est: ut in considerandis singulis vocibus alicuius orationis tantum tempus insumamus, quantum communiter una respiratio durare solet. Quod si quis pro sua devotione amplius morari vellet, poterit quidem; sed tunc potius ad secundum orandi modum pertinebit, quam ad hunc tertium. Iuvat autem hic modus, ut assuescamus facere orationem vocalem cum attentione et devotione debita, ut servemus illud Apostoli: Orabo spiritu, orabo et mente (1 Cor. 14, 15). Quare hoc exercitium est valde utile eis qui obligati sunt ad horas canonicas, vel ad alias orationes vocales.
paras.en: The third method of prayer is to be understood thus: that in considering each word of some prayer we spend as much time as one breath commonly lasts. If anyone, out of devotion, should wish to linger longer, he may indeed do so; but then it will belong rather to the second method of prayer than to this third. This method helps us to grow accustomed to making vocal prayer with due attention and devotion, so that we may keep the word of the Apostle: I will pray with the spirit, I will pray also with the mind (1 Cor 14:15). Hence this exercise is very useful for those who are bound to the canonical hours, or to other vocal prayers.

paras.la: Quamvis autem hi tres modi orandi hic tradantur, non existimandum est excludi alios modos, quos Spiritus Sanctus docere solet, et quos viri in spiritu exercitati secundum experientiam et secundum rationem et doctrinam sanam habere solent, vel quos quisque sibi utiles ad suum profectum ipso usu deprehenderit. Quod idem etiam de nostris ipsis intelligendum est — accedente tamen semper approbatione et consensu superioris vel praefecti spiritualis, quibus quisque patefacere modum debet quem in orando tenet, eoque magis si paulum discedat ab ordinario modo. Caeterum tres hi modi non solum alius aliis aptior erit pro personarum varietate, sed etiam persona eadem, pro varia dispositione animi vel corporis, aptior erit modo ad unum, modo ad alium: ut v. g. cum aliquis est fatigatus vel male habet, non erit bene dispositus ad longiorem meditationem et mentis excursum, et tunc magis iuvabitur secundo vel tertio modo. Quod intelligendum est non solum in hac quarta hebdomada, sed reliquo omni tempore.
paras.en: But although these three methods of prayer are taught here, it is not to be thought that other methods are excluded — those which the Holy Spirit is wont to teach, and which men practised in the spirit are wont to possess according to experience and according to reason and sound doctrine, or which each has found by use itself to be profitable for his own progress. The same is to be understood of our own members as well — always, however, with the approval and consent of the superior or spiritual prefect, to whom each ought to disclose the manner he keeps in praying, and the more so if he departs somewhat from the ordinary manner. For the rest, not only will one of these three methods be more apt than another according to the variety of persons; the same person too, according to the varying disposition of mind or body, will be more apt now for one, now for another: as, for example, when someone is fatigued or unwell, he will not be well disposed for longer meditation and mental excursion, and will then be more helped by the second or third method. And this is to be understood not only in this Fourth Week, but at all other times as well.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXVIII
kapitel.la_titel: De regulis tradendis
kapitel.en_titel: On the rules to be given

paras.rub: Cur positae regulae in fine exercitiorum
paras.la: Regulae quae additae sunt in fine exercitiorum non ideo positae sunt ut omnibus proponantur, sed ut quisque eguerit, vel etiam desideraverit pro sua devotione.
paras.en: The rules added at the end of the Exercises were not placed there in order to be proposed to all, but as each shall have need of them, or even desire them out of his own devotion.

paras.la: Quare illae quae agunt de distributione eleemosynarum non debebunt dari nisi iis qui locupletes sunt, et qui solent aut possunt eleemosynas facere. Similiter quae agunt de scrupulis, non est cur dentur iis qui nullis scrupulis agitantur.
paras.en: Hence those which treat of the distribution of alms should be given only to those who are wealthy, and who are accustomed or able to give alms. Likewise those which treat of scruples: there is no reason to give them to those who are troubled by no scruples.

paras.la: Eae item quae ad catholicam doctrinam pertinent, quamvis ad omnium pietatem confirmandam et fovendam valent, iis tamen potissimum qui in locis vel cum personis suspectis versantur, secundo loco omnibus etiam operariis, et iis qui verbum Dei tractant, tradendae sunt: quia directe pugnant contra sensa et dicta haereticorum nostri temporis.
paras.en: Those, again, which pertain to Catholic doctrine, although they avail to confirm and foster the piety of all, are nevertheless to be given above all to those who live in suspect places or among suspect persons, and in the second place also to all workers, and to those who handle the word of God: because they fight directly against the opinions and sayings of the heretics of our time.
paras.note: The reference is to the Rules for Thinking with the Church (Regulae ad sentiendum cum Ecclesia) at the end of the Exercises.

kapitel.label: Cap. XXXIX
kapitel.la_titel: Brevis explicatio nonnullorum, quae in Directorio de tribus viis attinguntur
kapitel.en_titel: A brief explanation of certain points touched in the Directory concerning the three ways

paras.rub: De viis purgativa, illuminativa et unitiva
paras.la: Quoniam in hoc Directorio, et in exercitiis tradendis, fit mentio viae purgativae, illuminativae et unitivae, et quod his respondent ordine suo hae quattuor hebdomadae, ideo visum est, pro maiori notitia huius rei, aliquid addere. Non enim hoc ita accipiendum est, ut intelligatur aliquis, peracta prima hebdomada, perfecte et plene purgatus; peracta autem secunda et tertia, perfecte illuminatus; et denique, absoluta etiam quarta, pervenisse ad plenam unionem cum Deo. Haec enim omnia indigent diuturno tempore, studio et exercitatione: in extirpandis vitiis, in passionibus edomandis, et in virtutibus acquirendis.
paras.en: Since in this Directory, and in the giving of the Exercises, mention is made of the purgative, the illuminative and the unitive way, and it is said that these four Weeks correspond to them in their order, it has seemed good, for the better understanding of this matter, to add something. For this is not to be taken as meaning that someone, having finished the First Week, is perfectly and fully purged; having finished the Second and Third, perfectly illumined; and finally, the Fourth also completed, has arrived at full union with God. All these things require long time, application and exercise: in rooting out vices, in taming the passions, and in acquiring the virtues.

paras.la: Verum hoc indicatur: primam hebdomadam proportione quadam respondere viae purgativae, quoniam in ea nihil aliud agitur quam ut peccata praeterita recogitentur et ponderentur, et concipiatur de eis quam maximus dolor et contritio, et timor aeternae poenae; ex quibus fiat ut animus abstrahatur ab amore omnis rei terrenae, et fundetur in odio et detestatione peccati. Quae omnia pertinent ad purgationem animae.
paras.en: What is indicated is rather this: that the First Week corresponds, by a certain proportion, to the purgative way, since in it nothing else is done than that past sins be thought over and weighed, and the greatest possible sorrow and contrition for them conceived, and the fear of eternal punishment; whereby the soul is drawn away from the love of every earthly thing, and grounded in the hatred and detestation of sin. All of which belongs to the purgation of the soul.

paras.rub: Secunda et tertia hebdomada partim purgativae, partim illuminativae
paras.la: Similiter in secunda et tertia hebdomada, considerando exemplum Domini Salvatoris tum in vita tum in passione, et omnes virtutes quae in eo tanquam in idea fulserunt, nos quoque discimus in quo consistat salus et perfectio hominis, et quae via sit ad aeternam beatitudinem consequendam. Et praeterea, cum anima purgata fuerit, fit habilis et apta ad recipiendas illustrationes divinas, et illapsum et influxum illius interni luminis; simulque gignitur in anima vigor quidam, eiiciens omnem concupiscentiam, eamque ferventem faciens ad patiendam paupertatem, contemptum et omnem asperitatem, et excutiens omnem negligentiam, et disponens ad exequenda bona opera vigilanter et strenue.
paras.en: Likewise in the Second and Third Weeks, by considering the example of the Lord and Saviour, both in his life and in his Passion, and all the virtues which shone in him as in their idea, we too learn in what the salvation and perfection of man consists, and what the way is to attaining eternal blessedness. And moreover, when the soul has been purged, it becomes fit and apt to receive the divine illuminations, and the entrance and inflow of that inward light; and at the same time there is begotten in the soul a certain vigour, casting out all concupiscence, making it fervent to endure poverty, contempt and every hardship, shaking off all negligence, and disposing it to carry out good works watchfully and strenuously.

paras.la: Denique in quarta hebdomada — primum ob resurrectionem et ascensionem Domini, in qua simul etiam meditari possumus futuram nostram gloriam, quoniam, ut ait Paulus, si Christus resurrexit, et nos resurgemus; deinde vero ex meditatione ad amorem in nobis excitandum, quae multiplex est et varia puncta ac materias complectitur — efficitur ut anima uniatur Deo per amorem: qui concipitur meditando bonitatem Dei et eius beneficia, et quantum nostra causa egerit atque pertulerit; tum etiam per desiderium coelestis gloriae; per considerationem praesentiae Dei in omni re et in omni loco; gaudendo de eius perfectionibus, et optando placere ei soli, idque propter ipsum solum; et nunc eum laudando, nunc magnificando, nunc admirando eius altitudinem, et aliis similibus, quae, ut ante diximus, respondent viae unitivae.
paras.en: Finally, in the Fourth Week — first by reason of the Resurrection and Ascension of the Lord, in which we can at the same time also meditate on our own future glory, since, as Paul says, if Christ has risen, we too shall rise; and then through the meditation for stirring up love in us, which is manifold and embraces various points and matters — it is brought about that the soul is united to God through love: a love conceived by meditating on the goodness of God and his benefits, and how much he has done and endured for our sake; then also through the desire of heavenly glory; through the consideration of the presence of God in every thing and in every place; by rejoicing in his perfections, and desiring to please him alone, and that for his own sake alone; now praising him, now magnifying him, now marvelling at his height — and other like things which, as we said before, correspond to the unitive way.

paras.rub: Ratio duplex cur hae quatuor hebdomadae respondere his viis dicantur
paras.la: Haec igitur est ratio duplex cur dicatur has quatuor hebdomadas respondere his tribus viis. Primum, propter materias quae in earum quaque tractantur, pertinentes ad has vias; et quia in eis iaciuntur initia singularum, quae deinde oportet prosequi cum tempore et cum studio, si velimus ad aliquam earum perfectionem pervenire. Deinde etiam quia discitur modus ac methodus quam deinde servare debemus in prosequenda unaquaque harum viarum.
paras.en: This, then, is the twofold reason why these four Weeks are said to correspond to these three ways. First, because of the matters treated in each of them, which pertain to these ways; and because in them the beginnings of each are laid, which must then be pursued with time and application if we wish to arrive at any perfection in them. And second, because the manner and method is learned which we must afterwards keep in pursuing each of these ways.

paras.rub: An semper in una permanendum, an ad priores redeundum
paras.la: Ex his ergo sequitur quod, etiam si quis aliquem gustum aut specimen huius viae unitivae in quarta hebdomada habuit, non propterea debet assidue in ea haerere, sed debet redire ad priores vias, et sese diu et ordinarie continere tum in passionum mortificatione, tum in virtutum exercitatione, et in aliis eiusmodi studiis consentaneis utrique viae. Etsi nihil impedit — immo etiam saepe evenit — ut, dum aliquis versatur in una via, sentiat interdum aliquos affectus pertinentes ad aliam viam; nec sunt reiiciendi, modo, ut dictum est, non exerceantur ordinarie ante tempus.
paras.en: From this it follows, then, that even if someone has had some relish or foretaste of this unitive way in the Fourth Week, he ought not on that account to cling to it continually, but should return to the earlier ways, and keep himself long and habitually both in the mortification of the passions and in the exercise of the virtues, and in other such pursuits belonging to both those ways. Yet nothing prevents — indeed it often happens — that while someone is engaged in one way he sometimes feels certain affections belonging to another; nor are these to be rejected, provided, as has been said, they are not practised habitually before their time.

paras.la: Hoc enim negocium non ex spatio temporis, sed ex mensura profectus pendet. Nam si quis temere aspirare vellet ad illam viam unitivam, esset magna confusio, quae impediret omnino profectum spiritualem, et insuper etiam esset res exposita periculis et illusionibus. Faceret enim perinde ac si quis ex infima schola transire vellet ad primam, non transeundo per medias; aut si ex infimis gradibus scalarum saltu traiicere vellet ad summos, relictis iis qui sunt interiecti. Sic igitur, antequam aliquis exerceat se ex professo in via hac quam diximus unitiva, oportet ut bene purgatus sit exercitiis viae purgativae, et deinde etiam bene profecerit in via illuminativa. Ex huius enim defectu provenit ut multi, non ambulantes sed saltantes in via Domini, post multum tempus diversosque labores vacui virtutibus inveniantur: impatientes et iracundi, et cum aliis eiusmodi imperfectionibus.
paras.en: For this business depends not on the span of time, but on the measure of progress. If anyone were rashly to aspire to that unitive way, there would be great confusion, which would altogether hinder spiritual progress; and the thing would moreover be exposed to dangers and illusions. He would be acting as if someone wished to pass from the lowest class of a school to the first without passing through those between; or as if from the lowest steps of a staircase he wished to leap across to the highest, leaving out those that lie between. So then, before anyone exercises himself professedly in this way we have called unitive, he must be well purged by the exercises of the purgative way, and then also have made good progress in the illuminative. For from the lack of this it comes about that many, not walking but leaping in the way of the Lord, are found after much time and diverse labours empty of virtues: impatient and irascible, and with other imperfections of that kind.

paras.la: Immo hic gradus ad altiorem viam non tam ex electione nostra et voluntate ac conatu pendet, quam ex directione Spiritus Sancti, cuius mos est ascensiones istas in anima disponere, ut eat de virtute in virtutem. In quo tamen, ad certiorem directionem et ad praecavendos errores qui contingere possunt, consulendus est pater spiritualis qui animam gubernat, et cum eius consilio in omnibus procedendum.
paras.en: Indeed, this step to the higher way depends not so much on our own choice and will and effort as on the direction of the Holy Spirit, whose manner it is to dispose these ascents in the soul, that it may go from virtue to virtue. Yet in this, for surer direction and to guard against the errors that can occur, the spiritual father who governs the soul is to be consulted, and one should proceed in everything with his counsel.

kapitel.label: Cap. XL
kapitel.la_titel: Quae commendanda sunt ei qui absolvit exercitia
kapitel.en_titel: What is to be commended to one who has finished the Exercises

paras.la: Ut qui ex loco calido ad locum frigidum egreditur, facile fieri potest ut cito frigefiat, nisi diligentem curam adhibeat retinendi calorem: ita qui, exercitiis peractis, redit ad communem vitam et conversationem, nihil est facilius quam ut fervorem ac lumen conceptum brevissimo tempore perdat — praesertim quia quicquid boni acquisivit nondum est confirmatum per modum habitus, sed est tanquam passio quaedam, quae facile remittitur, vel etiam tota amittitur. Quod cum contingit, omnis fructus et omnis labor exercitiorum evanescit.
paras.en: As one who goes out from a warm place into a cold one may easily grow cold quickly unless he takes diligent care to retain his warmth: so for one who, the Exercises finished, returns to common life and intercourse, nothing is easier than to lose in a very short time the fervour and light he has conceived — especially because whatever good he has acquired is not yet confirmed after the manner of a habit, but is like a passion, which is easily weakened, or even wholly lost. And when that happens, all the fruit and all the labour of the Exercises vanishes.

paras.la: Quare hoc primum commendandum est ei qui exercitia absolvit: ut magni aestimet hoc principium et quasi fundamentum vitae bonae et spiritualis, quod per Dei gratiam iecit in exercitiis; idque a Deo accipiat tamquam beneficium, et quidem maximum; et omnia lumina, omnem cognitionem quam in exercitiis acquisivit, credat sibi a Domino Deo donata peculiari quodam amore, et ut talia ea conservare et tueri studeat. Praeterea timorem concipiat, ne, si deinceps non vixerit ut intellexerit esse vivendum, gravius a Deo puniatur ob ingratitudinem: et quia scienti bonum et non facienti maius iudicium est ipsi.
paras.en: Therefore this is the first thing to be commended to one who has finished the Exercises: that he set great store by this beginning and, as it were, foundation of a good and spiritual life which by God's grace he has laid in the Exercises; that he receive it from God as a benefit, and indeed the greatest; and that all the lights, all the knowledge he acquired in the Exercises, he believe to have been given him by the Lord God out of a certain particular love, and strive to preserve and guard them as such. Moreover, let him conceive a fear lest, if hereafter he does not live as he has understood he ought to live, he be punished more heavily by God for ingratitude: for to him who knows the good and does not do it, the greater is the judgment upon him.

paras.la: Secundo loco intelligat se adhuc nihil aliud fecisse, nisi quod bonum semen in eius anima a Deo seminatum est. Unde, nisi hoc semen foveatur et excolatur et ad maturitatem perducatur, ut det fructum in tempore suo, per se quidem aut nihil aut parum est. Itaque hoc primum cavere debet: ne eiusmodi semen vel a volucribus, id est a daemonibus, rapiatur, vel a spinis suffocetur — nempe a cogitationibus et cupiditatibus terrenis et vitiosis. Ideoque non solum peccata, sed etiam eorum occasiones evitet, et illa praesertim ad quae ante exercitia inclinatus fuit: nam contra haec potissimum se armare debet, quia facillime recidere potest.
paras.en: In the second place, let him understand that as yet nothing else has been done than that good seed has been sown by God in his soul. Hence, unless this seed is cherished and cultivated and brought to maturity, so as to give its fruit in its season, of itself it is either nothing or little. So he must first beware lest such seed either be snatched away by the birds — that is, by the demons — or be choked by the thorns, namely by earthly and vicious thoughts and desires. Let him therefore avoid not only sins but also their occasions, and especially those to which he was inclined before the Exercises: for against these above all he must arm himself, because he can most easily fall back.

paras.la: Tertio hortandus est ad conservandam et alendam devotionem iam conceptam piis et spiritualibus exercitationibus, inter quas haec potissimum commendari poterunt. Primo, ut conservet usum meditandi quotidie per dimidiam horam, aut etiam integram, si fieri poterit. Secundo, ut singulis diebus faciat examen conscientiae per quartam horae partem. Tertio, ut octavo quoque die confiteatur et communicet. Quarto, eligat aliquem confessarium stabilem, eumque accipiat ut ducem huius spiritualis itineris, et cum eo tractet omnia quae ad suam animam pertinent. Quinto, legat saepe pios libros, et habeat bonorum hominum conversationem, malorum autem fugiat summopere. Sexto, curet proficere quotidie in virtutibus, praesertim in humilitate, patientia et charitate. Et in summa nitatur ipse quoque ad eam summam perfectionem, quam in suo statu, et iuxta mensuram divinae gratiae, acquirere poterit.
paras.en: Third, he is to be exhorted to preserve and nourish the devotion already conceived by pious and spiritual practices, among which these above all may be commended. First, that he keep the practice of meditating daily for half an hour, or even a whole hour if it can be done. Second, that every day he make an examination of conscience for a quarter of an hour. Third, that every eighth day he confess and communicate. Fourth, that he choose a fixed confessor, and take him as guide of this spiritual journey, and treat with him of everything that concerns his soul. Fifth, that he often read devout books, and keep the company of good men, and flee that of the bad with all his might. Sixth, that he take care to advance daily in the virtues, especially in humility, patience and charity. And in sum, let him too strive after that highest perfection which, in his own state and according to the measure of divine grace, he shall be able to attain.

paras.rub: Praeter generalia monita, sunt alia peculiaria
paras.la: Haec autem sunt fere generalia monita, quae omnibus dari poterunt. Alia sunt deinde quae iuxta cuiusque professionem, aut statum, aut particularem indigentiam addi poterunt; immo haec ipsa augeri et intendi ex maiori aliquorum devotione et progressu spirituali: quod facile advertet bonus et prudens instructor, adiutus gratia et lumine Domini et Salvatoris nostri Dei — cui sit gloria et honor in saecula. AMEN.
paras.en: These, then, are roughly the general counsels that can be given to all. There are then others which may be added according to each one's profession, or state, or particular need; indeed, these very ones may be enlarged and intensified according to the greater devotion and spiritual progress of some: which a good and prudent instructor will easily perceive, aided by the grace and light of our Lord and Saviour God — to whom be glory and honour for ever. AMEN.

paras.la: Ego Virgilius Ceparius, Rector Collegii Florentini Societatis Iesu, legi hoc directorium exercitiorum P. Ignatii, et nihil in eo reperi contra fidem aut bonos mores. Florentiae, die 1. Septembris 1599. — Imprimatur Florentiae, die 2. Septembris 1599. Alexander Caccia, Vicarius Florentinus.
paras.en: I, Virgilio Cepari, Rector of the Florentine College of the Society of Jesus, have read this directory of the Exercises of Father Ignatius, and have found nothing in it against faith or good morals. Florence, 1 September 1599. — Let it be printed. Florence, 2 September 1599. Alessandro Caccia, Vicar of Florence.
paras.note: The censor's attestation and the imprimatur of the Florence printing, retained here as part of the historical document.
